HG Discover is seeking a knowledgeable and engaging **Stock Market & Investing Instructor** to develop and teach beginner-friendly classes covering stock market fundamentals, investing strategies, financial literacy, and long-term wealth building.

The ideal candidate has a strong understanding of financial markets and a passion for helping individuals develop the knowledge and confidence needed to make informed financial decisions.

Classes may be designed for teenagers, young adults, and adults, including individuals with disabilities and participants with little or no previous investing experience.

Introduce investment accounts, brokerage platforms, and retirement savings concepts.  
Teach risk management, diversification, compound growth, and long-term investing principles.

Introduce the differences between investing, trading, and speculation.

Experience in investing, financial education, banking, accounting, economics, financial planning, or related fields.

Experience teaching, coaching, mentoring, or facilitating workshops.

Strong communication and presentation skills.  
Commitment to financial inclusion and community education.

Certified Financial Planner (CFP)  

Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA)  
Relevant FINRA securities registrations  
Degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, or Business  

Qualified self-directed investors and experienced financial educators are also encouraged to apply.

HG Discover offers a flexible instructor revenue-sharing model.

Instructors may receive **60%–70% of eligible class revenue**, depending on the negotiated partnership agreement.

**Illustrative earning potential:**

5 students: Approximately $50–$70 per teaching hour  

8 students: Approximately $80–$110 per teaching hour  
10 students: Approximately $100–$140 per teaching hour

Flexible class scheduling.  

Opportunity to create and lead your own financial education curriculum.  
Potential classroom and administrative support.  
Opportunity to promote financial literacy in underserved communities.  
Ability to develop recurring classes and educational workshops.  
Meaningful work helping participants understand investing and financial decision-making.  
Opportunity to grow with a developing community education initiative.  

How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit a résumé or professional background summary outlining their investing knowledge, financial education experience, and teaching qualifications.

Selected candidates may be invited to an introductory interview and facility tour.

**Help community members understand the market, build financial confidence, and invest in their financial education!**

**HG Discover — Learn. Create. Move. Grow.**

*This is an educational instructor opportunity, not a position to provide personalized financial advice. Engagement is subject to applicable screening, agreed compensation terms, and a written instructor agreement.*

Bilt is the membership for where you live.

The Fund for Public Health in New York City (FPHNYC) is a 501(c)3 non-profit organization that is dedicated to the advancement of the health and well-being of all New Yorkers. To this end, in partnership with the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH), FPHNYC incubates innovative public health initiatives implemented by DOHMH to advance community health throughout the city. It facilitates partnerships, often new and unconventional, between government and the private sector to develop, test, and launch new initiatives. These collaborations speed the execution of demonstration projects, effect expansion of successful pilot programs, and support rapid implementation to meet the public health needs of individuals, families, and communities across New York City.
  
  
 Our Culture

About The Role
  
The GAC Fund Project Coordinator will work under the direction of the GAC Project Manager to administer the NYC GAC Fund portfolio. The GAC Fund Project Coordinator is part of the team primarily responsible for citywide efforts to promote and protect access to gender affirming care.
  
  
About the Program
  
Gender-affirming care (GAC) is recognized by major U.S. medical associations as medically necessary for many transgender and gender-diverse people. In addition, many transgender and gender non-conforming/non-binary (TGNCNB) individuals also need legal or practical assistance in updating their identification documents, combatting jobs or housing discrimination, or even accessing education or bathrooms. Research shows GAC is associated with reduced depression and suicidal ideation, and better long-term mental health outcomes. Denial of care or legal recognition of one’s identity increases risk of mental health crisis and unsafe self-treatment. Yet access has become increasingly difficult due to state-level restrictions, insurance barriers, and shifting federal guidance.
  
  
New York City has been an innovator and leader in sexual and reproductive health. The New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene has long followed the tenets of the Sexual and Reproductive Justice Framework which states that all people should have the power and resources to make healthy decisions about their bodies, including sexuality and reproduction.
  
  
As part of these efforts, the Health Department will develop and implement a new fund to contract with clinical providers to ensure access to care for youth in need of gender-affirming care. This funding will enable providers of youth gender-affirming care to address financial shortfalls resulting from any denials or reductions in federal funding and increase their capacity to ensure continuity of care for medically necessary hormone therapy for transgender youth in accessible and affordable care settings.

description:
**A day in the life**
---------------------

You start your morning by preparing the daily shipping and receiving manifest, then spot-check incoming raw-material deliveries against purchase orders to ensure every receipt is properly supported. Before lunch, you review laminating job bags to confirm materials are allocated to the right jobs, and you verify that all material issues flow accurately through production and into work-in-process (WIP). You’ll also manage any return-to-vendor (RTV) items and organize job bags and sheeting paperwork so everything is audit-ready.

Midday is about partnering with operations: you facilitate a weekly production waste meeting and help implement reduction strategies, calculate and oversee production KPIs used for the incentive plan, and run weekly audits of finished goods and subassembly materials. You’ll keep physical inventory and cycle-count programs on track, including valuation and obsolescence reviews, and manage customer-supplied inventory usage for each receipt and order.

Afternoons often shift toward the close: processing billing and accounts payable invoices, maintaining WIP values for the trial balance, reconciling inventory stock status to the trial balance, and ensuring standard costs are current. At month-end, you complete cost and inventory accounting activities, calculate the monthly COGS to align expenses with revenue, prepare and submit the gross-profit report, and support the close schedule and balance-sheet analysis. You’ll also review and close manufacturing jobs once production is complete, perform consolidation and intercompany reconciliations, support quarterly and annual audits by bank and financial auditors, and take on miscellaneous accounting projects as assigned.

* **Communication and Executive Collaboration:** Excellent analytical, organizational, communication, and decision-making skills, with the ability to communicate complex technical risks and recommendations to executive leadership and business stakeholders.

Executive-Level Expectations

The successful candidate is expected to combine extensive professional experience with advanced technical expertise and strategic leadership capabilities. This position requires the ability to manage complex cybersecurity operations, lead multidisciplinary teams, establish enterprise security standards, and align cybersecurity initiatives with the organization's long-term business objectives.

* You communicate clearly and can turn detailed analysis into a compelling recommendation
* You’re excited by the opportunity to work directly with a Founder and take on increasingly broad ownership as the company grows
* You’re authorized to work in the United States
* You’re excited to be in-person in New York City 5 days a week

You’ve spent several years in investment banking or another rigorous finance environment and have since moved into strategic finance, business operations, or a similar role at a high-growth startup.

* Highly motivated, ambitious, and capable - you want to tackle large, meaningful problems and hold yourself to a high bar
* Ownership mindset - you think long-term and put the business and our customers first
* High velocity and high excellence - you move with urgency without sacrificing the quality of your work

* Meaningful equity ownership

* Beautiful, sunshine and snack-filled office in the heart of Flatiron, Manhattan

Our team exists to ask hard questions about those vulnerabilities, and to seek out strategies for protecting democratic freedoms — in the short and long term, through both technical and policy levers.
 This is early, high-stakes research. The team is small, the problems are genuinely unsolved, and the work will matter.
 We are looking for someone with deep expertise in both AI and at least one of: law, government, political science, or public policy.  Projects on this team are illustrative rather than fixed — we expect the research agenda to evolve as both AI capabilities and institutional pressures change. Current and expected focus areas include:

title: Business Analyst - Health Insurance
description:
Accountabilities
As Business Analyst, you will act as the link between business departments and IT teams, ensuring that insurance requirements are accurately understood, documented, and translated into practical solutions. Your responsibilities will include:
- 
 Analyze business requirements and operational processes within the Swiss health and accident insurance sector.
- 
 Develop appropriate solutions in collaboration with business stakeholders and IT specialists.
- 
 Manage requirements throughout the full lifecycle, including analysis, concept development, specification, implementation, and validation.
- 
 Contribute to the continuous improvement of insurance applications and business processes, particularly claims processing and automated invoice verification.
- 
 Ensure the functional and technical quality of applications, supporting error analysis and resolution when needed.
- 
 Configure and maintain insurance applications, including keeping reference data and tariff information accurate and up to date.
- 
 Participate in customer projects and coordinate release planning and implementation with customers, business teams, developers, and system providers.
- 
 Monitor legislative and regulatory developments in the Swiss insurance market and identify the resulting business and system requirements.
 Requirements
 The ideal candidate combines a solid understanding of health insurance operations with strong business analysis and requirements engineering capabilities. You should be comfortable working independently while collaborating with a range of business and technical stakeholders. The following qualifications are expected:
- 
 Degree or professional training in business informatics, computer science, or a commercial discipline, supported by strong IT affinity.
- 
 Several years of professional experience in the Swiss health and/or accident insurance sector.
- 
 In-depth knowledge of claims processes under the Swiss Health Insurance Act (KVG) and/or Insurance Contract Act (VVG).
- 
 Experience with insurance tariffs and tariff-related processes is an advantage.
- 
 Proven experience in business analysis, requirements engineering, and the analysis, design, and specification of business requirements.
- 
 Familiarity with insurance applications, ideally Adcubum Syrius or Sumex.
- 
 Experience configuring applications; knowledge of SQL is an advantage.
- 
 Knowledge of software testing, quality assurance, or release management is a plus.
- 
 Independent, structured, and solution-oriented working style.
- 
 Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with different stakeholders.
- 
 Excellent written and spoken German, with a professional communication style.

 Remote working arrangement, open to candidates worldwide.

 Fixed-term employment contract.

 Opportunity to contribute to projects within the Swiss health and accident insurance sector.

 Potential to work across business analysis, insurance application optimization, and IT implementation.

description:
ABOUT US

Sparrow is the first high-tech, high-touch employee leave management solution. Our mission is to make it simple for companies to provide their employees with all kinds of leave (i.e. family, medical, etc.).

Currently, the leave management process is painful and inefficient for everyone. Company leaders struggle to keep up with regulations and processes that change frequently, and the employees going on leave are overwhelmed by bureaucracy at an exceptionally important juncture in their career. Sparrow transforms this ordinarily tedious, error-prone, complex to remain compliant, and time-consuming process into a 30-minute end-to-end experience saving teams time (20 - 40 hours per leave) and money (up to $30K per leave).

Sparrow is headquartered in San Francisco but all employees work remotely across the country. Sparrow is a diverse, highly talented, and supportive team. Together, we are hardworking, collaborative, smart, and humble—after all, we’re solving real problems.

About The Team And Role

You'll be Sparrow's first Strategic Finance hire, reporting directly to the CFO. This is an opportunity to build the finance function from scratch: owning the models and analysis that drive real decisions. You'll partner directly with the CFO on strategy while independently owning execution, and you'll have real influence on how this function is built as Sparrow scales.

What You'll Do

 - Model Ownership: Own all financial models, including the operating model, headcount model, and other models that set goals and measure business performance across the company.

 - Build the next-generation Strategic Finance function: Develop AI-powered workflows, automated analyses, and intelligence systems that redefine what a small strategic finance team can do.

 - Strategy: Assess and define our existing and potential future strategic priorities. Quantitatively validate and drive influence toward the highest revenue impact and ROI initiatives.

 - Reporting and Insights: Deliver data-driven insights and recommendations that inform go-to-market tactics, product decisions, budget allocations, Board of Directors and investor materials, leadership reporting and other cross-functional roadmaps.

 - Business Partnership: Collaborate with cross-functional partners across Sales, Engineering, Product, Operations, and Leadership.

 - 3-5 years of experience, whether from investment banking, consulting, or in-house FP&A or strategic finance. Experience with consumption-based or usage-based business models is a meaningful plus.

 - You identify problems before they're handed to you, and you thrive when the answer isn't obvious.

 - An A-player mindset with a strong bias for action: you raise the bar, move with urgency, stay resilient through ambiguity, and take ownership to deliver meaningful outcomes.

 - Comfortable being the only one in the room who does this. There's no existing Strategic Finance team to lean on yet, you're helping to build the first version of it.

Compensation

This is a full-time salaried position with compensation of $97,000-$143,000 depending on experience and location.

Our work at Sparrow is impactful. We help People teams with one of the hardest parts of their job, and we support employees at a time when they need it most. We’re driven by our mission, much like a nonprofit, but with the resources and scale of a fast-growing venture-backed company.

We offer a competitive salary and equity, comprehensive health, vision, and dental insurance options, and a generous employer 401(k) match.

As a healthcare technology company, Ellipsis Health may conduct background checks on candidates who receive an offer, in accordance with applicable law. We evaluate every candidate holistically and comply with all applicable "ban the box" regulations.

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

We are partnering with a venture-backed artificial intelligence company based in San Francisco developing frontier AI systems specialized in institutional financial reasoning and quantitative analysis.

Rather than relying on simple debt templates, the platform evaluates AI systems on their ability to build and audit dynamic debt mechanics from the ground up.

In this role, you will serve as a Credit & Debt subject-matter expert. Working entirely from a blank spreadsheet in Excel, you will build, stress-test, and document institutional-grade credit models. Your completed workbooks, formulas, and written step-by-step logic will serve as the verifiable ground-truth datasets used to train, benchmark, and fine-tune AI models against institutional lending standards.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Blank-Sheet Debt Modeling: Construct integrated credit, debt sizing, and repayment models completely from scratch in Excel without relying on pre-built templates, plug-ins, or automation tools.

 - Complex Debt Schedules & Sculpting: Build dynamic multi-tranche debt schedules (senior secured, mezzanine/subordinated, revolving facilities, unitranche, PIK notes) including mandatory amortization, cash sweeps, interest capitalization, and prepayment mechanics.

 - Cash Flow Available for Debt Service (CFADS): Model and stress-test core coverage and leverage metrics, including DSCR, LLCR, PLCR, interest coverage, and net debt-to-EBITDA ratios across varying business cycles.

 - Covenant & Downside Stress-Testing: Construct multi-variable sensitivity tables and downside scenarios to evaluate default probabilities, covenant headroom, breakeven cash flows, and liquidation/recovery outcomes.

 - Structural Credit Logic: Build collateral and borrowing base mechanisms (e.g., eligible receivables/inventory, advance rates, concentration limits, and reserves).

 - Ground-Truth Logic Documentation: Provide clear, structured written explanations in English detailing the credit rationale, structural protections, formula mechanics, and accounting relationships embedded in each model.
   
   


MUST-HAVE REQUIREMENTS

 - 2–8+ years of direct experience in Private Debt, Credit Funds, Leveraged Finance, Direct Lending, Project Finance, Rating Agencies, or Credit Risk / Underwriting.

 - Demonstrated "From-Scratch" Excel Mastery: Proven ability to build full, auditable debt schedules and cash flow models from a blank workbook using disciplined financial modeling standards (e.g., FAST or institutional credit equivalents with zero circularity errors).

 - Advanced Credit Mechanics: Hands-on experience structuring cash flow waterfalls, principal repayment schedules, covenant compliance checks, and reserve accounts (e.g., DSRA).

 - Deep Financial Accounting Knowledge: Solid command of 3-statement financial statements (US GAAP / IFRS) and how working capital swings, Capex, and operational shocks flow directly into cash available for debt service.

 - Full-Time Dedication: Availability to commit 35–40 dedicated hours per week on an ongoing basis.

 - Written Communication: Fluent professional English with the ability to clearly articulate credit risk logic, covenants, and mathematical steps in writing.
   
   


NICE-TO-HAVE QUALIFICATIONS

 - Asset-Based Lending (ABL): Experience modeling borrowing bases, advance rates, dilution, and collateral-driven credit facilities.

 - Structured Finance / ABS: Experience with tranched waterfalls, loss distributions, credit enhancements, and prepayment/default curves.
   
   


WHY JOIN?

 - Shape AI in Credit Analysis: Directly influence how frontier AI models understand risk, debt structures, and credit underwriting.

 - True Autonomy: 100% remote and fully asynchronous—structure your working hours around output milestones.

 - Competitive Global Pay: Consistent monthly contractor compensation reflecting your depth of technical credit modeling and weekly output.

 This role sits at the intersection of Pricing & Commercial Operations and Finance, providing commercial insights and analytics to support Gross-to-Net (“GTN”) management across Pfizer’s U.S. Hospital Injectable and Biosimilar portfolio, with a primary focus on pricing, contracting and chargebacks. You will analyze contracting terms, pricing dynamics, and chargeback trends to assess and communicate their impact on GTN, revenue, margin, and overall profitability.
 In this high-impact role, you will develop and analyze chargeback, rebate, admin fees, and other key GTN assumptions, identify business drivers and trends, and translate complex price-related contracting activity into clear, actionable insights for stakeholders across Commercial and Finance. You will support forecasting and planning and help strengthen understanding of how commercial decisions translate into financial performance.
 The role will also help advance automation and AI-enabled analytics to improve the speed, transparency, and quality of GTN analysis, forecasting, and decision-making.

 Pricing Impact Analytics & Support 
- Provide analytics to inform GTN assumptions, with a primary focus on contracting and chargebacks, and advise stakeholders on the impact of 340B, Medicaid, and other key GTN drivers on revenue and profitability.
- Support chargeback accrual pipeline calculations and related analytics using Finance- and Controllership-approved methodologies and assumptions.
- Analyze contracting activity, claims, utilization, pricing trends, and other commercial data to identify emerging trends and assess potential impacts to GTN and revenue forecasts.
- Compare commercial assumptions with actual experience, identify key drivers of variance, and provide business rationale and analytics to support forecast refinement and decision-making.

- Partner with Finance to inform GTN forecasts by providing commercial assumptions, analytics, and insights related to contracting, chargebacks, payer/channel mix, pricing actions, and new product launches.

- Model the GTN, revenue, and profitability impact of contracting strategies, including bids, committed contracts, off-cycle price actions, channel strategies, and business development initiatives, to inform decisions before they are finalized.

- Ensure data integrity between the contract management system (Flex) and the corporate ERP; optimize use of chargeback and script-level data and third-party aggregators to improve rebate validation and forecast accuracy.
- Drive automation, scalable dashboards, and reporting improvements — leveraging AI-enabled tools responsibly, with appropriate governance and human oversight, to shift capacity toward insight generation.

 DoorDash’s mission is to grow and empower local economies. By building intelligent, last-mile delivery technology for local cities, DoorDash connects people with the local businesses they care about — helping grow businesses and the communities that support those businesses.  We're looking for a Research Operations Manager to be the operational backbone of our research team, and a driving force behind DoorDash's commitment to customer obsession. Every great product decision starts with a real voice: a Dasher, a merchant, a customer. You'll own the systems, tools, vendors, and AI-powered processes that get those voices in front of the people building for them, faster and at greater scale. You'll also champion a culture of experimentation and continuous improvement, so the research practice keeps getting better along with our understanding of the people we serve. This is a high-impact role at the intersection of research, operations, and technology, built for someone who sees friction before it's surfaced and treats it as theirs to solve.

- Positions the extensive capabilities of Merrill and Bank of America

title: Financial Services Transfer Pricing Strategist

description:
Who we are 
 About Stripe 
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. 
 About the team 
 Stripe’s Tax Transfer Pricing team designs, implements, and defends the intercompany pricing policies that support Stripe’s global operating model, ensuring pricing between Stripe entities is compliant, defensible, and aligned with how the business creates value.
 As Stripe expands its product portfolio and international footprint, our transfer pricing policies and documentation must evolve alongside the business. Transactions between Stripe affiliates are becoming increasingly complex and, in some cases, share characteristics with transactions commonly undertaken by financial services institutions. These arrangements, including those supporting Stripe’s stablecoin-related activities, may also be subject to scrutiny from regulators that oversee the financial services sector. We are seeking an experienced Transfer Pricing Specialist with financial services expertise to help develop practical, scalable transfer pricing policies, work through the tax and regulatory considerations relevant to intercompany arrangements, and provide subject matter expertise in audit defense and dispute resolution.
 What you’ll do 
 The Financial Services Transfer Pricing Strategist will be a hands-on, collaborative member of the team responsible for developing and implementing compliant, practical transfer pricing policies and processes. The role will focus on transactions between Stripe’s legal entities that have characteristics commonly associated with the financial services sector, including intercompany arrangements supporting Stripe’s stablecoin-related activities.
 This individual will work closely with teams across the organization and must be an excellent communicator who can explain complex transfer pricing concepts clearly to non-tax audiences. The ideal candidate will have transfer pricing experience in payments, fintech, banking, or another regulated financial services environment, as well as a track record of partnering effectively with cross-functional teams and other members of the tax organization.
 Responsibilities 
- Partner with teams within and outside of Finance to develop, execute, and maintain transfer pricing policies for Stripe’s current and future operating structure and product offerings with a strong moral compass and integrity
- Analyze financial information to design, prepare, and review detailed calculations, assist in preparing legal entity forecasts, and support the tax provision process
- Address the transfer pricing impacts of special projects related to restructurings, acquisitions, and corporate initiatives, and ensure operating models are fit for purpose in the context of evolving global tax and transfer pricing frameworks and other regulations that apply to transactions between affiliates

About the Role

Industrious signs new landlord partnerships every year, and the number is growing as our business development team expands. Before any of those deals move forward, someone has to check that it holds together: that the assumptions are sound, that the start date, budgets, rent, pricing, and returns all track, and that the figures from design and construction have carried through correctly. As a Real Estate Associate on our Real Estate Transactions team that will be your job!



You will underwrite assigned deals in Excel, explain what drives their returns, and flag where a deal is tight, whether on pricing, occupancy, or CapEx. Our business development colleagues make the call on whether a deal goes ahead, and your analysis is what they rely on to make it well. You will work with Design, Construction, Finance, and other teams to make sure every number is right, supporting several business development colleagues as deal flow shifts.



Our approach to underwriting is different from a traditional real estate shop, and we will teach it to you. In your first few months you will get close review and clear guidance while you learn how we work. You will also join at a good time: the team is growing, new roles are being added, and we are underwriting a new product, so there is real room to learn, ask questions, and grow with us.



Success here means accurate work. The team trusts your numbers, your flags are clear, and any mistake you make happens once, not twice.



What Might Your Day Look Like

Your morning starts with a new deal from one of our business development colleagues. You go through the model piece by piece: the start date, the budget, the rent and revenue share assumptions, the cash flows, the IRR, and the margin the location is expected to earn per rentable square foot. title: Business Operations Generalist, Finance & Accounting
description:
ABOUT WONDERLY

Wonderly is a closed-loop, end-to-end system that self-improves on our customers’ revenue. We serve the home service industry ($1.3T), and can consistently double a new customer’s revenue within 90 days. We make all of our AI and software completely free - and only get paid when our customers make real money. We’re here helping real small businesses make a life, pay for their children’s college tuition, and live the American dream.

Pre-AI SaaS sold tools. AI companies claim they sell outcomes - task done, call answered, lead booked, ticket resolved - but calls or leads aren’t the outcomes that ultimately matter. Revenue is what ultimately matters, and today, none of the AI companies actually promise revenue. Wonderly changes that.

Our 70-person team (mostly in PDE) spent over a year building in stealth; our thesis is that - if you actually want to control the end result (revenue) of a business and deploy AI fast/cheaply, you can’t just build the sexy part (agents), you must also build the unsexy parts and own everything end to end: the system of record layer and the application layer. We built from scratch every software a home service business needs - replacing ServiceTitan, Squarespace, Ringcentral, Jobber, Square, Hubspot, and a dozen others applications. And we built every agent necessary - AI marketing, AI receptionist, AI voice, AI sales outreach, AI sales coaching, AI follow-ups, AI 3D design, AI finance, AI quoting, AI collections, and more - all embedded inside our own system with native data access. As a result, we can deploy dozens of production-ready Agents to our customers in under 24 hours with no FDEs, no integrations, and no data cleaning work.

We are the most outcome driven business model in the business because we’ve proven our system and AI Agents actually work in driving the end result - revenue. We are not trying to sell our customers a dream - each of our 10+ core AI Agents help improve our customers’ revenue by 5-20%.

Wonderly already has PMF and has gone from 0 → 1 (we are happy to share more over a call), with very clear moat and deep industry knowledge that took a team of 70 hardcore A-players 18 months to build (we are at least 2 years ahead of anyone else in the space). We believe Wonderly has the potential to be a $100B - $1T outcome. The market is massive https://www.acquired.fm/episodes/home-depot: home service businesses across North America (a $1.3T market). We’ve raised over $50M from top-tier investors, have $20M a year in free cashflow from another product line (Motion), and all that money gets pumped into Wonderly.




ABOUT THE HIRING MANAGERS

Hi, we’re Chander and Harry, Wonderly’s CTO and CEO.

You’ll report directly to one of us. We’re looking for someone we can trust to own the operational details that keep Wonderly running—from getting the numbers right to working through a vendor contract or fixing a broken process.

You don’t need to have seen every problem before. You do need to ask good questions, exercise sound judgment, and follow through. As you build context and earn trust, you’ll take on more ownership across the business.




THE ROLE

We’re hiring someone to own the financial and business operations behind Wonderly.

Accounting is roughly a third of the role. You’ll make sure vendors get paid correctly, coordinate month-end close with our external accountants, and keep tax requirements and financial systems organized. The rest spans contracts, procurement, insurance, equity administration, and the operational problems that come with a growing company.

We want someone with an accounting foundation who wants broad business ownership. You should be comfortable investigating an unfamiliar charge, working through a vendor renewal, coordinating with outside counsel, and building a process so the same issue is easier next time.

Your responsibilities will include:

 - Accounting operations: Validate invoices, collect vendor documentation, coordinate approvals, and schedule payments.

 - Month-end close: Keep close notes, provide supporting information to our accountants, investigate discrepancies, and flag unusual transactions.

 - Tax coordination: Keep filings, registrations, notices, and year-end reporting moving with our external providers.

 - Financial systems: Maintain tools such as Stripe, Subscript, Hubifi, and QuickBooks as the business changes.

 - Contracts and procurement: Coordinate agreements with business owners and counsel, negotiate vendor terms, and track commitments and renewals.

 - Corporate operations: Manage insurance renewals, routine equity administration, corporate records, registrations, and incoming notices.

 - Process improvement: Document recurring work, establish clear owners and deadlines, and work with our internal team to automate repetitive tasks.

You’ll have recurring responsibilities and unexpected problems. You’re accountable for closing the loop on both.




WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE DIFFERENT

You’ll work directly with our CTO or CEO and see how decisions get made across the company.

Your accounting knowledge will give you a starting point, but your scope will extend across finance, legal, procurement, and corporate operations. You’ll work with accountants, lawyers, brokers, vendors, and internal teams—and be responsible for making sure work gets finished.

You’ll also have room to improve how the company operates. When something takes ten manual steps, we want you to question it, understand the constraints, and help build a better system.

As you become someone the company trusts with increasingly complex problems, your responsibilities can grow with you.




BACKGROUNDS THAT TEND TO WORK

People from these backgrounds could thrive here:

 - Accounting or finance operations at a fast-growing startup.

 - Public accounting with hands-on exposure to startup clients.

 - Business operations roles with meaningful accounting responsibilities.

Why We Exist

Your car and your home are your most important assets, yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every part of the journey — buy/sell, insurance, maintenance, repairs — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

 

Jerry.ai http://Jerry.ai is building the first app to manage it all. We started with car insurance in 2019, became one of the top 3 brokers in the U.S., then added driving insights, diagnostics, and a repair marketplace.

Our Business Operations & Analytics  team has been a force multiplier and accelerant to our business that has helped us reach these pivotal milestones in spite of headwinds and within a highly competitive market. They are a team of former McKinsey, BCG and Bain consultants who drive data & insights, and inform decision-making across every corner of our business. They are analytical powerhouses and first principles problem solvers who push forward our most important initiatives across product, growth, tech, and operations.

 

Every business unit has a Business Operations & Analytics team member embedded within it  —  someone who doesn't just run analyses and build dashboards, but shapes what questions we should ask, what data to pull, what conclusions to draw, what decisions to make, and then drives our teams towards our next goal: go from 5M to 50M customers and become a $10B business in the next 4 years. 

 

As our business continues to expand, there is growing demand for more Business Operations & Analytics team members. We are hiring 2-3 people to drive impact in these areas:

 - Growth Marketing 

 - Product Development

 - Strategic Partnerships 

 

On leveling: You may see job ads for this role at different job levels. Our priority is finding the right people, we can be flexible with job title/leveling.

 

Why You Will (Or Won't) Like Working Here

 - No slides: If you've worked in consulting, you know what it feels like to be up at 3am reformatting a deck. That doesn't exist here. The only work that gets done at Jerry is work that will materially change the trajectory of our business — an important product, a new growth channel, a key metric, a critical partner relationship, etc. 

 - No corporate fluff: The Business Operations & Analytics team is 14 insatiable learners who care deeply about solving difficult problems and making a tangible impact. Every person owns a critical domain. There is no bloat, unnecessary meetings, or waiting for approvals. 

 - Hands-on: This is not a pure strategy role, you will also own execution. Your day-to-day will be surfacing analytical insights, driving decisions, and seeing them through end-to-end. 

 

What You'll Own

You'll sit on our central Business Operations & Analytics team but you’ll be embedded in one of Jerry's core business areas — growth, product, AI and automation, strategic partnerships — and own the analytical function for that business unit end-to-end.

 - Define the right problems: Before any analysis, understand what business question it's answering and what decision it will inform. Push back if the question is flawed.

 - Data and insights: Define metrics, build reports, run analyses, design experiments, and surface data insights that move your team's key metrics.

 - Drive outcomes: Bring recommendations to your counterparts in product, growth, finance or operations, tell them what's happening and why, and what next steps should be.

 

Who You Are

 - First principles thinker: You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses before touching data. You're analytically strong (comfortable with SQL or Python) but your instinct is to ask "what are we trying to solve here?" before jumping to "what should I build?" 

 - Direct communicator: You can walk a skeptical stakeholder through a complex finding and get buy-in quickly. You write clearly, speak precisely, and don't bury the lede.

 - Owner: You act like your name is on the door. If something is broken, you feel responsible for fixing it, even if it’s outside of your swim lane.

 

What You'll Bring

 - 2+ years of experience at a consulting firm, investment bank, or high-growth technology company.

 - Strong analytical skills; ability to pull, structure, and interpret data independently.

 - Track record of owning ambiguous problems and delivering impact.

 - Clear, persuasive communicator who can influence decisions at the leadership level.

 

Our Tools

SQL (Clickhouse), Metabase, Python, Jupyter Hub, GitHub.

Basis https://www.basis.ai is a nonprofit applied AI research organization with two mutually reinforcing goals.

The second is to advance society’s ability to solve intractable problems. This means expanding the scale, complexity, and breadth of problems that we can solve today, and even more importantly, accelerating our ability to solve problems in the future.

 - Cost model: Own cost per deliverable hour by channel, market, and product with our FP&A and operations teams, so every price we quote and every rate we pay starts from what the data costs us.

 - Deal performance: Track every signed deal against its model, report actual margin and cash by customer and partner, and feed what you learn back into pricing and the forecast.

 Blue Rose Research is hiring a Policy Fellow to help design an economic plan for the AI era: a concrete policy agenda for how the country should respond as AI changes jobs, wages, and the economy. The Policy Lead will own the policy substance of the plan. They will identify its key choice points, such as how to support workers whose jobs change, how to share the gains from AI, and how to pay for it, develop realistic options for each, and work through those trade-offs with our research team.

- Lead development of the AI economic plan, from first framework to final proposals

- Draw on existing research and proposals on automation, labor markets, the social safety net, workforce training, tax policy, and competition
- Draft policy memos, option papers, and the plan itself
 Working with the Research Team 
- Turn policy options into concrete proposals our research team can test with voters through polling and message testing

 Expert & Government Engagement

description:
ABOUT OPEN STANDARD

Open Standard is on a mission to build the world's best money, starting with the US dollar. We believe money should move the way data does: instantly, globally, at any hour, in any amount.

Our flagship product, Open USD (OUSD) https://ousd.xyz/, is a stablecoin built for the internet. It's live on Ethereum, Base, Solana, and Tempo, with Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe, and Visa as founding partners and 200+ companies in our network.

We're a lean team in San Francisco and New York, led by Zach Abrams, who co-founded Bridge and previously led product at Brex, Coinbase, and Square.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring our Banking and Financial Institutions Lead: the person who brings OUSD to banks, asset managers, exchanges and the rest of traditional finance.

This is a sales role, and a long-term bet. Our model should change how dollars move through the financial system, and that change runs through institutions that move carefully. You'll plug OUSD into flows that either don't exist yet or that we're replacing, which means long, education-heavy cycles with many counterparties at the table.

You'll own a large surface area of banks and capital markets firms, mostly on your own from day one. That means daily meetings with institutions, learning fast what works and what doesn't, and seeing complex deals through to signature.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own OS's relationships with banks, asset managers, exchanges, and capital markets players.

 - Build and run a pipeline of institutional deals from first meeting to signed agreement.

 - Represent Open Standard with senior leaders at large financial institutions.

 - Map every deal's counterparties (business sponsors, risk, compliance, legal, treasury, operations, technology) and get each of them to yes.

 - Shape use cases with partners, such as stablecoin settlement, collateral, and treasury flows, and turn them into a clear value proposition.

 - Educate institutions on stablecoins and OUSD, and turn their objections into product and policy feedback for the team.

 - Work closely with our capital markets, partnerships, policy, and product teams.

 - Help define how we sell to TradFi as the team grows.


WHO YOU ARE

 - 7 to 15 years selling to banks and other financial institutions, with a track record of closing large, complex deals.

 - You know how banks buy: who signs, who can block, how risk and compliance reviews work, and how long it really takes.

 - Fluent in institutional and trading-focused clients, and in the language of Wall Street and TradFi.

 - A strong network across banks and capital markets, and the credibility to get a meeting with senior decision makers.

 - Experience with stablecoins, digital assets, or payments infrastructure.

 - Polished in the room, scrappy outside it. You drive deals forward even when the other side moves slowly.

 - Comfortable working with a high degree of independence and no existing playbook.

 - Low ego, high ownership, and direct.

 - Already using AI tools in how you research, prepare, and sell.

About Us
 At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

 Our team researches web application attacks and turns that research into protections in Cloudflare’s Web Application Firewall (WAF). We build and maintain managed rules that help protect millions of Internet properties from known vulnerabilities, emerging exploits, and new attack techniques.

Using threat intelligence and telemetry from Cloudflare’s global network, we identify exploitation patterns, develop mitigations, and measure how well they work against real traffic. We partner with Engineering, Product, and customer-facing teams to improve coverage while minimizing false positives and disruption to legitimate applications.

- You make evidence-based tradeoffs between detection coverage, false positives, and performance. You are comfortable investigating ambiguous reports and following issues through to resolution.

 Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. By continuing to innovate and deliver for our customers, we have become a household name and the must-have mobile-based membership for families (and those friends who are basically family).
 Life360 has more than 500 (and growing!) remote-first employees. For more information, please visit life360.com .
 Life360 is a Remote First company, which means a remote work environment will be the primary experience for all employees. All positions, unless otherwise specified, can be performed remotely (within the US and Canada) regardless of any specified location above.  
 We are AI Native
 We are building an AI native company where AI is an integral part of how we build and operate. AI tool usage during interviews varies by role. You may be asked to demonstrate proficiency with AI tools, discuss how you leverage AI, or complete interview exercises without AI assistance. Your Recruiter will provide clear guidance as you move through the interview process.
 Undisclosed use of AI not previously discussed with or approved by your Recruiter may impact your candidacy.
 About The Team
 The Data & Analytics Team (DnA) is a 60+ person organization spanning data engineering, analytics engineering, analytics/decision science, and data science/ML. The science teams are organized into two sub teams, focusing on MAU and Revenue. This role leads decision science and data science within MAU.
 You and your team will be responsible for understanding the drivers behind MAU: why members come, why they stay, and why they return. The team partners with product, marketing, and engineering to put those learnings into everyday work, and that work shapes our roadmaps.
 Our data is unusual for a consumer company. Life360 measures families and circles rather than individuals, so one member's behavior affects another's, which makes measurement a different problem than a standard funnel. With billions of location events, driving behavior, crash detection, and Tile and Pet GPS trackers, we get a rich picture of physical behavior that few consumer companies can build.
 About the Job
 We're hiring a Staff Decision Scientist to lead Advanced Analytics: the methods, models, and standards the rest of the data team builds on. You won't be embedded in a single Operating Group (OG). You'll work across all of them, pushing how we run experiments and establish causality, and owning the MAU forecast and growth model that leadership uses to plan the business. You'll report into the Data & Analytics leadership team.
 Most of your impact will come through other people. You'll partner closely with Decision Scientists, Data Scientists, Analytics Engineers, and Data Engineers, and you'll use AI to make advanced methods repeatable, so rigor doesn't depend on whether you personally touched the project. This is not a production ML role (we have a dedicated Data Science / MLE team for that). Your primary tools are statistical inference, forecasting, clear thinking, and the judgment to know which method fits the question.
 In your first year, success looks like an experimentation and causal inference standard the team has adopted, and an MAU forecast with tracked accuracy that leadership uses for planning.

We take into consideration an individual's background, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience in determining final salary. Base pay may also vary based on geographic location, with US work locations falling into one of three geographic tiers.

 Department Overview 
The Product Orderability team sits at the intersection of Go-To-Market Strategy, Product Management, and Sales. We drive end-to-end orderability workflows across Motorola Solutions product lines and ensure CPQ configuration stability. 
Our mission is to enable a seamless, sales-first user experience by simplifying configuration rules, maintaining platform stability and accelerating New Product Introduction (NPI) cycle times to ensure global sales teams can quote and order solutions effortlessly. 
Job Description
 We are seeking a proactive and tech-savvy Business Analyst (Oracle CPQ) to bridge the gap between our business stakeholders and technical execution teams. In this role, you will play a key part in gathering, analyzing, and transforming complex product requirements into robust configuration solutions within Oracle CPQ . 
 Additionally, we are looking for a forward-thinking candidate with hands-on experience utilizing modern AI tools (e.g., Google Gemini, ChatGPT) to streamline requirement drafting, automated test case generation, workflow optimization, and data analysis.

- Requirement Gathering & Management: Partner with cross-functional stakeholders (Product Owners, Sales, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Factory teams) to define product scope and translate business requirements into detailed technical specifications for Oracle CPQ.

- BOM & Structure Simplification: Reduce ordering complexity by simplifying Bills of Materials (BOMs), rule logic, and offering structures in close collaboration with Product Management and Engineering. 
- Portfolio Optimization: Drive SKU reduction, product cancellation analysis, and offer/catalog simplification activities. 
- Development & Testing Alignment: Partner directly with developers to clarify business requirements, answer functional queries, and perform validation/testing post-development.

- Agile Execution: Operate effectively within an Agile team environment to gather and analyze requirements while delivering high-quality ERP/CRM implementations.

- Programming & Querying Knowledge: Technical understanding or hands-on experience with SQL, PL/SQL, or scripting languages (e.g., Google Apps Script, BML, or Python) is preferred. 
- Oracle Ecosystem Experience: Prior experience with Oracle Enterprise Applications (such as Oracle EBS, Oracle PLM, or Oracle CPQ Admin features) is preferred. 
- Domain Experience: Background or knowledge in the Telecommunications domain is preferred. 
- Adaptability & Mentorship: Ability to learn new technologies quickly, become an operational subject matter expert, solve complex business problems, and teach or mentor others. 
- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field (preferred). 
- Experience: Minimum 1-3 years of strong experience in a Business Analyst role gathering requirements, defining scope, and creating functional specifications for Oracle CPQ . 
- AI Tool Proficiency: Hands-on experience using modern AI tools (e.g., Google Gemini) for writing requirements, streamlining business process modeling, or generating test scripts. 
- BOM Knowledge: Strong understanding of Bills of Materials (Oracle ERP) and rule-based configuration models. 
- Process Modeling: Proven experience creating business process models and using them to clearly describe functional business requirements.

Job Description Summary 
You will lead the enterprise people and organization agenda for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DSAI) across Novartis, translating our DSAI ambition into the workforce, organization, talent and capability choices needed to deliver it. Operating at the decision-making table with senior DSAI leaders and partnering across the enterprise, you will shape how we build, attract and grow critical DSAI talent, strengthen our external value proposition, and enable responsible human-AI collaboration. You will lead the enterprise DSAI OTR, including discussion at ECN level, and create the standards, governance and frameworks needed in areas such as careers, capabilities, talent and rewards, particularly where established approaches do not yet exist.
This enterprise role complements rather than replaces the Workforce Strategy Leads directly supporting DSAI teams within their units. Unit-level accountabilities remain unchanged, while this role connects across them, providing the overarching DSAI people strategy, standards and governance and enabling enterprise-level choices where these are needed. 
 Job Description 
 #Hybrid 
 This role can be based in Cambridge, East Hanover, London or Basel, please only apply to one of the appropriate location.
 Key Responsibilities 
- Set the enterprise DSAI people and organization strategy.
Translate the DSAI ambition into an integrated, future-ready agenda across workforce, organization, leadership, culture, talent and capability. Success is evident when: enterprise priorities and accountabilities are clear, adopted across units, and translated into measurable outcomes. 
- Shape strategic workforce and capability choices. Use scenarios, analytics, external insight and data storytelling to anticipate demand for scarce DSAI capabilities and recommend choices on organization design, skills, capacity, location, sourcing and workforce mix. Success is evident when: critical gaps are addressed before they constrain innovation or execution. 
- Lead the enterprise DSAI OTR. Orchestrate the enterprise talent review, integrate perspectives across units, and present implications, choices and recommendations to ECN. Success is evident when: pivotal talent, succession, capability risks and enterprise actions are visible and actively managed. 
- Establish enterprise talent and career approaches. Create differentiated career development, mobility, succession and talent-allocation mechanisms suited to DSAI roles and communities. Success is evident when: Novartis can attract, develop, deploy and retain pivotal DSAI talent across organizational boundaries. 
- Build the external DSAI talent brand and pipeline. Strengthen Novartis’ visibility as an employer of choice through targeted engagement with universities, specialist talent networks and external forums. Build early-talent pathways that attract dual technical/scientific and DSAI expertise and develop judgement, experience and leadership capability. Success is evident when: Novartis has stronger external visibility and a sustainable pipeline of scarce DSAI talent. 
- Design and create enterprise DSAI standards. Build new governance, rewards approaches, career architecture, capability frameworks, talent programs and operating approaches for a field evolving faster than established internal practices. Success is evident when: scalable standards replace fragmented local approaches and remain relevant as DSAI evolves. 
- Connect enterprise strategy and unit execution. Define decision rights, interfaces and governance so the enterprise mandate is distinct from, and complementary to, unchanged unit-level P&O accountabilities. Success is evident when: there is no duplication or accountability gap between enterprise and unit roles. 
- Influence a complex enterprise stakeholder system. Partner with at least nine ECN-1 leaders across R&D, Commercial, Operations and Global Functions, the Head of GDC, unit P&O Business Partners and Expertise Hubs to resolve enterprise trade-offs without relying on formal authority. Success is evident when: leaders move beyond unit optimization and commit to enterprise decisions. 
- Redesign work for human-AI collaboration. Guide organization, role and workflow choices that enable responsible collaboration among people, automation and AI agents while sustaining accountability and a human-cantered employee experience. Success is evident when: adoption improves productivity, innovation and decision quality. 
- Coach senior leaders, shape culture and lead transformation. Challenge and coach leaders through ambiguity, build commitment to new enterprise approaches, anticipate resistance and track adoption and benefits. Success is evident when: leadership behaviour, culture and ways of working support the DSAI strategy. 
 What you’ll bring to the role
 Essential Criteria 
- Extensive experience of progressive P&O/HR experience, including strategic partnership with executive and ECN-1 leaders in a complex global matrix. 
- Strong organization design, strategic workforce planning and transformation experience, including scenario development and enterprise trade-off recommendations. 
- Demonstrated experience creating global or enterprise-wide people strategies, standards, governance or programs, not only implementing established solutions. 
- Evidence of leading enterprise talent reviews, succession and capability discussions with senior executive forums. 
- Demonstrated ability to influence multiple senior stakeholders across business units, functions, countries and P&O disciplines without formal authority. 
- Fluency in people analytics and confidence with AI-enabled tools, responsible AI principles and emerging work technologies. 
 Desirable Criteria 
- Experience translating emerging technology, data science or digital strategy into workforce, organization and talent implications; direct DSAI sector experience is highly desirable. 
- Relevant university degree or equivalent exp

DeployCo is being built from the ground up as a subsidiary of OpenAI and funded with a partnership of outside investors.



About the Role

We are seeking a Finance Data Analytics Senior Manager to build and own the data foundation for DeployCo’s AI-native FP&A function. Reporting to the FP&A lead, you will combine hands-on data skills with finance expertise to build reliable pipelines, maintain trusted datasets, analyze performance, and deliver clear recommendations. You will own the full finance data lifecycle, from connecting source systems and defining financial metrics to explaining business results. Working with FP&A, Accounting, and cross-functional teams, you will support budgeting, rolling forecasts, revenue and pipeline analysis, headcount and capacity planning, and management reporting. This is a hands-on role for someone who is equally comfortable writing SQL, troubleshooting a data pipeline, and explaining a financial analysis. You will build and maintain the underlying systems and use the data yourself to answer business questions, identify risks and opportunities, and recommend actions as the finance function grows.

This role is based in New York City.



In this role, you will:

 -  Build and maintain finance data pipelines and models connecting ERP, planning, CRM, HRIS, and project delivery systems, with consistent financial metric definitions.

 - Own data quality and reliability through monitoring, troubleshooting, source reconciliations, automated checks, documentation, and access controls. 

 - Analyze revenue, margins, pipeline conversion, and workforce capacity; explain performance drivers and variances, and maintain models for budgeting, forecasting, and scenario analysis. 

 - Deliver clear management reporting and enable self-service analysis through trusted datasets, dashboards, and documented metrics that help finance and business teams answer their own questions.

 - Use Codex and ChatGPT to analyze finance data, develop recommendations, and automate recurring workflows, validating code, calculations, and conclusions and keeping outputs traceable. 

 - Partner with FP&A, Accounting, IT, Engineering, and business teams to prioritize finance data needs, use approved platforms, and support tool adoption.



You may thrive in this role if you:

 - Bring approximately 6–10 years of relevant experience across finance, FP&A, accounting, analytics, data engineering, or finance systems, with meaningful hands-on experience in both finance and data.

 - Have personally built and maintained data pipelines and financial datasets used for recurring analysis and reporting, including ongoing troubleshooting and support.

 - Bring strong SQL and practical proficiency in Python or a comparable scripting language, with experience integrating APIs, querying databases, and automating data transformations.

 - Have a strong understanding of financial statements and hands-on experience in budgeting, forecasting, and revenue, cost, margin, and variance analysis; can explain the business drivers behind the numbers.

 - Have practical experience with data modeling, ETL/ELT, cloud data warehouses, and scheduled workflows; can turn inconsistent source data into reliable, well-documented finance datasets.

 - Apply sound data quality and control practices, including source reconciliations, automated checks, version control, documentation, and appropriate access to sensitive finance data.

 - Communicate clearly with finance, technical, and business stakeholders; translate ambiguous questions into analyses and recommendations, and explain assumptions and limitations.

 - Take ownership from initial build through ongoing maintenance, analysis, and reporting, prioritizing business needs and improving processes as the finance function grows.

Blossom Health exists to solve the mental health epidemic in America by partnering with psychiatrists to expand access to affordable, timely, clinically-effective mental healthcare. Our AI-native care platform is loved by hundreds of clinicians and thousands of patients.

We’re a Series A company with $20M+ raised from Headline, Village Global, and the founders of General Catalyst, Flatiron Health, Sword Health, Grow Therapy, Fay, Elemy, Zip, Blank Street, Assured, Bridge, Birches Health, and Enzo Health.

We’re looking for a Strategic Finance & Business Operations Lead to own the financial and analytical work behind some of Blossom’s most important business decisions.

This is not a generalist BizOps role. You’ll spend a significant amount of your time digging into the economics of the business: understanding our revenue structure, building financial models, evaluating new opportunities, and turning complex financial and operational data into decisions.

You’ll report directly to our Founder and work closely with leaders across the company as we scale.

 - 🚀 Be early in a hyper-growth startup: Join the foundational team of a rapidly scaling company and help build the financial and operational infrastructure behind our next stage of growth

 - 🧠 Talent-dense team: Work alongside a top-percentile team with high standards, intellectual curiosity, and a shared ambition to build something consequential

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Own financial analysis and modeling across revenue, growth, unit economics, and strategic initiatives

 - Develop a deep understanding of Blossom’s revenue structure and identify opportunities to improve the economics of the business

 - Build models and analyses that inform company-level decisions around growth, investment, resource allocation, and new opportunities

 - Partner with the Founder and business leaders on high-priority strategic and operational projects

 - Translate complex financial and operational data into clear recommendations and actionable decisions

 - Build reporting, forecasting, and analytical processes as the company scales

 - Evaluate new business opportunities, partnerships, markets, and strategic initiatives from both a financial and operational perspective

 - Move beyond the analysis when needed and help execute on the opportunities you identify


YOU'LL BE A GOOD FIT IF:

 - You have 2–6 years of professional experience, with a strong foundation in finance and financial analysis

 - You’re excited by the opportunity to work directly with a Founder and take on increasingly broad ownership as the company grows

 - You’re authorized to work in the United States

 - You’re excited to be in-person in New York City 5 days a week

Bonus: You’ve spent several years in investment banking or another rigorous finance environment and have since moved into strategic finance, business operations, or a similar role at a high-growth startup.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

 - Highly motivated, ambitious, and capable - you want to tackle large, meaningful problems and hold yourself to a high bar

 - Ownership mindset - you think long-term and put the business and our customers first

 - High velocity and high excellence - you move with urgency without sacrificing the quality of your work

 - Analytically rigorous - you’re comfortable going several layers deeper than the obvious answer

 - An explorer - you’re comfortable with ambiguity, autonomy, and questions that don’t have an existing playbook

 - Humble - you use your strengths in service of the team and understand that success is an output, not an input

 - $120,000–$180,000 base salary

 - Meaningful equity ownership

 - Significant growth opportunities as the company scales

 - Beautiful, sunshine and snack-filled office in the heart of Flatiron, Manhattan

 - Health, dental, and vision insurance

 - A focus on outcomes, not hours

 - Team outings, offsites, and unlimited PTO

description:
ABOUT US

JOB SUMMARY

The Senior AI Deployment Manager, Finance brings strong finance-domain experience to client work that applies AI to accounting and finance workflows. You will lead client discovery and delivery workstreams, turn unclear process needs into a practical implementation plan, and partner with Forward Deployed Engineers to move the work forward.

The priority areas are order-to-cash, month-end accounting close, and procure-to-pay. You should understand how finance teams operate and have implemented AI workflows in real work. Deep accounting process judgment matters more than AI specialization; you should be able to learn new tools quickly, explain their limits, and bring engineering in where technical decisions require it.

Eliza works AI-first and expects everyone in the company to use AI tools thoughtfully in their work. Client priorities move quickly, and the work can be ambiguous. You will receive ownership of a workstream, not a fixed script, and will be expected to communicate risks and tradeoffs early.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


1. LEAD FINANCE DISCOVERY AND PROCESS MAPPING

 - Run client sessions to understand the finance outcome, users, current process, systems, data, controls, exceptions, and pain points.

 - Focus discovery on O2C, month-end close, and P2P; establish the facts needed to assess value and feasibility.

 - Identify which process steps are suitable for AI, where conventional automation is a better fit, and where human judgment must remain.


2. DEFINE A PRACTICAL IMPLEMENTATION PLAN

 - Translate finance needs into product requirements, prioritized MVP scope, acceptance criteria, and a work plan an FDE can build against.

 - Make dependencies, access needs, data quality, risks, and assumptions explicit.

 - Recommend a sequence that balances business value, feasibility, timing, and quality.


3. OWN THE DELIVERY WORKSTREAM

 - Manage scope, milestones, client decisions, risks, handoffs, and status through testing and client review.

 - Partner closely with an FDE, keeping business requirements and technical decisions aligned without taking over engineering ownership.

 - Evaluate workflow performance using agreed test cases and success criteria; surface failure modes and propose next steps.


4. BUILD CLIENT CONFIDENCE AND ADOPTION

 - Facilitate working sessions with finance SMEs and communicate progress and tradeoffs in clear language.

 - Present concise updates that distinguish verified results from estimates or hypotheses.

 - Help client teams understand the workflow, its limitations, review requirements, and operational handoffs.


5. CONTRIBUTE TO THE FINANCE DELIVERY PRACTICE

 - Support finance-focused pursuits and scope discussions with grounded process and implementation judgment.

 - Coach Associates or teammates on client delivery and finance-workstream execution where assigned.

 - Package reusable discovery questions, process maps, requirements patterns, and delivery lessons.


QUALIFICATIONS


REQUIRED

 - Strong finance-domain experience in finance transformation, program finance, corporate finance, or a related field.

 - Practical knowledge of at least one of order-to-cash, month-end close, or procure-to-pay. Experience in AP/AR, invoicing, ERP, or finance systems is relevant.

 - Evidence of implementing AI-supported workflows in real work; casual AI tool use alone is not enough.

 - Can translate finance process requirements into clear implementation considerations and partner effectively with engineers.

 - Working understanding of AI capabilities and limitations, with sound judgment about human review and operational risk.

 - Strong writing, presentation, stakeholder management, and prioritization skills.

 - Finance transformation consulting or professional-services delivery experience.

 - FP&A, program finance, or analytical experience.

 - Controller, CPA, or accounting-operations background.

 - ERP implementation, finance automation, or finance-focused AI product experience.

 - Experience in a PE-backed company.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation (base salary + performance incentives tied to client outcomes).

 - Equity options in a growing AI services company.

 - Exposure to a wide range of industries and high-impact AI problems.

 - Travel opportunities for on-site client engagements (if desired)

 - Close partnership with engineers and finance leaders on real operational problems.

 - The opportunity to shape reusable methods for finance AI delivery.

title: Senior Manager, Accounting & Finance
description:
Why Thunderbird? 
 Thunderbird is one of the world’s most trusted open-source email applications, empowering more than 20 million people globally. At Thunderbird, we build privacy-respecting communication and productivity tools that help people manage their digital lives while staying in control of their data. 
 We are open source by design. Our products are developed transparently and in collaboration with a global community of contributors, and that same spirit shapes how we work: collaboratively, inclusively, and with a shared commitment to putting users first. 
 We are a small but growing company of 70+ people distributed across seven countries. As Thunderbird evolves beyond a single desktop application, we are expanding across desktop, mobile, paid services, and new product experiences that help people and organizations work more effectively without giving up control to big tech ecosystems. 
 Our revenue model combines user donations, which help keep Thunderbird’s apps freely available, with paid services that cover the costs of hosted offerings while supporting long-term sustainability and continued innovation. 
 A note about Thunderbird and Mozilla: Thunderbird Technologies Corporation is the nonprofit-owned company behind Thunderbird email and a growing portfolio of products. While part of the Mozilla family, Thunderbird is a separate entity from Mozilla Corporation and Mozilla Foundation with its own compensation programs, benefits, and employment policies. 
 To learn more, visit www.thunderbird.net 
 The opportunity 
 We are looking for a Senior Manager, Accounting & Finance to serve as Thunderbird’s most senior finance professional. The right person will bring a strong accounting or controllership foundation and the breadth to lead financial planning and analysis, finance operations, and organization-level decision support. 
 As Thunderbird grows across donations, subscription services, enterprise offerings, and international operations, our financial needs are becoming more complex. We need stronger integration across accounting and FP&A, experienced oversight of emerging revenue models and tax obligations, and clear financial analysis that helps leadership understand performance, risks, tradeoffs, and decisions. 
 Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Head of Finance will directly manage our Senior Staff Accountant and Senior FP&A Analyst. This is a hands-on functional leadership role for someone who can provide experienced financial judgment, develop an established team, and remain close to the details while helping build the systems, controls, reporting, and finance practices the organization needs for its next stage of growth. 
 This role requires regular working-hour overlap with the COO, finance team, and other colleagues across North American time zones. Candidates based in Eastern or Central time zones are preferred; candidates elsewhere in the United States should be comfortable maintaining substantial overlap with those working hours. Flexibility for meetings with colleagues, advisers, and affiliated organizations in Europe is also expected. 
 What you’ll do  
- Lead Thunderbird’s finance function, with overall responsibility for accounting, financial planning and analysis, tax, treasury, and finance operations . 
- Manage and develop Thunderbird’s finance team , establishing clear priorities, responsibilities, review practices, and accountability . 
- Oversee monthly and annual close, financial reporting, reconciliations, accounting policies, and internal controls. 
- Oversee accounting and revenue recognition across donations, subscriptions, enterprise arrangements, partnerships, and other revenue streams. 
- Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, longer-range financial planning, and scenario analysis. 
- Develop clear management reporting and visualizations that highlight important trends, risks, tradeoffs, and decisions. 
- Oversee tax, audit, indirect tax, VAT/GST, corporate filings , and related work with external advisers. 
- Evaluate the financial, tax, accounting, and operational implications of entering new jurisdictions or establishing additional entities . 
- Work with Enterprise Partnerships and Legal to establish financial reporting, reconciliation, and control processes for partner-led commercial arrangements . 
- Oversee financial reporting to Thunderbird’s parent organization and affiliated Mozilla organizations. 
- Own financial oversight of payroll across multiple providers in partnership with the People team. 
- Document and strengthen finance systems and workflows, including accounting, expense management, payment-platform reconciliation, documentation, and automation. 
- Oversee cash-flow planning, treasury, banking, and investment activities, working closely with the Senior FP&A Analyst. 
- Serve as a trusted finance adviser to organizational leaders, translating complex financial information into clear recommendations . 
 What you bring  
- 15+ years of relevant professional experience, including progressively responsible roles spanning accounting, financial planning and analysis, and finance operations. 
- Significant accounting or controllership experience, including responsibility for U.S. GAAP financial reporting, close processes, internal controls, revenue recognition, and complex accounting judgments. 
- 5+ years of people management experience in a finance or accounting environment, including coaching, feedback, prioritization, performance support, career development, and team development. 
- Demonstrated ability to improve budgeting, forecasting, management reporting, and financial data visualization and translate complex information into clear insights and recommendations for non-finance leaders. 
- Substantive experience with subscription, SaaS, digital-product, enterprise, or comparable technology-based revenue models. 
- Experience supporting partner-led commercial arrangements, such as reseller, licensing, wholesale, or reve
