FINANCIAL OPERATIONS @ CLAY

Clay is looking for a Financial Operations Lead to join our growing Finance & Accounting team. This role will own the day-to-day financial operations that keep the business running smoothly, with a primary focus on accounts payable, employee spend, T&E, vendor management, and cash operations.

You’ll be responsible for building scalable processes and infrastructure across these areas as Clay continues to grow. This includes managing the full AP and expense lifecycle, partnering closely with employees and vendors, improving workflows and controls, and helping ensure our financial operations can scale with the business.

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys being hands-on, building from the ground up, and improving processes in a fast-moving environment. You’ll work closely with the broader Accounting, Finance, People, and Operations teams and have significant ownership over how financial operations evolve at Clay.



This role can be in our NYC or SF office with a hybrid set up. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Accounts Payable & Vendor Operations

 - Own the full AP lifecycle, including invoice intake, coding, approval routing, and timely payment processing

 - Manage vendor onboarding, maintenance, and documentation

 - Partner with vendors and internal stakeholders to resolve invoice and payment issues

 - Maintain accurate AP records and ensure processes are audit-ready

 - Reconcile AP activity to the general ledger and investigate discrepancies

 - Identify opportunities to automate and improve AP workflows as the company scales

description:
OWN YOUR INTELLIGENCE

 

Prime Intellect is building the open superintelligence stack: the infrastructure frontier AI labs build internally, made available to every ambitious AI team.

 

Our platform, Lab, unifies compute, environments, evaluations, secure sandboxes, high-performance training, and deployment into one full-stack system for post-training at frontier scale - from SFT and RL to tool use, agent workflows, and continuously improving production models. We are building open frontier AI: open-source models trained end to end for long-horizon tasks like autonomous research, and the full-stack platform our own research team uses to build them. The next generation of AI companies, enterprises, and research teams do not just need more GPUs. They need the ability to turn their own workflows, tools, data, and feedback loops into superintelligence they own.

 

Prime Intellect has raised $150M in total funding from Founders Fund, Radical Ventures, NVIDIA, and exceptional AI, infrastructure, and enterprise operators — including Andrej Karpathy, Dwarkesh Patel, and leaders and founders from Ramp, Perplexity, Harvey, Mercor, Zapier, Datadog, Cognition, OpenAI, Thinking Machines, Together AI, SemiAnalysis, LangChain, Browserbase, Cloudflare, Sierra, Databricks, Airbnb, OpenRouter, Standard Intelligence, Fleet, Core Auto, and more. We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of frontier research, real infrastructure, and go-to-market for a category that does not fully exist yet.


ROLE IMPACT

Quantitative finance is a demanding setting for agentic reinforcement learning: observations are noisy and non-stationary, actions have delayed and path-dependent consequences, naive objectives invite exploitation, and a convincing historical result can disappear under costs, constraints, or a new regime. You will build environments, evaluations, agents, and post-training methods for quantitative research and systematic decision-making. We have active programs with quantitative funds and other finance teams. The work may span research agents, market and portfolio simulators, time-series reasoning, execution, risk, and the production feedback loops that connect hypotheses to deployed systems.


RESPONSIBILITIES

Applied Research at Prime

We turn a workflow into tasks, environments, evaluations, and reward signals, run post-training experiments against real baselines, and deploy what works. When a result looks good, we find out whether the gain came from the model or from the data, harness, inference, or infrastructure. The reusable parts become shared research, open-source systems, and product capabilities.

Every Applied Research role is externally facing. Most researchers work directly with customers, users, or research partners while maintaining a substantive research agenda.

Representative early problems

 - Build a quantitative-research environment where an agent forms a hypothesis, writes and runs analysis, runs a backtest on point-in-time data, diagnoses the result, and decides what to test next.

 - Design rewards and evaluations that distinguish durable improvement from the artifacts of look-ahead bias, data leakage, overfitting, favorable execution assumptions, or hidden concentration and tail risk.

 - Train long-horizon agents to use data, research, coding, simulation, and portfolio tools while preserving provenance, respecting risk constraints, and adapting when market conditions change.

What you will own

 - Environments grounded in point-in-time data, realistic market mechanics, transaction costs, latency, capacity, and operational constraints.

 - Agents that conduct quantitative research, use analytical and execution tools, inspect their evidence, and recover from failed hypotheses.

 - Verifiers and evaluations that test robust out-of-sample behavior across assets, horizons, regimes, and adverse conditions.

 - Production loops with monitoring, human authority, regression gates, and failure attribution across models, data, simulation, and infrastructure, producing methods that transfer to other noisy, high-stakes decision systems.


REQUIREMENTS

 - We are looking first for depth in RL, agents, or post-training systems and the ability to become fluent in quantitative research.

 - Prior work in systematic trading, market microstructure, time-series modeling, econometrics, or financial simulation is useful but not required.

 - Hands-on experience building and debugging model-training, post-training, agent, evaluation, or closely adjacent experimental loops.

description:
ABOUT US:

Camber builds software to improve the quality and accessibility of healthcare. We streamline and replace manual work so clinicians can focus on what they do best: providing great care. For more details on our thesis, check out our write-up: What is Camber? https://camberhealth.notion.site/What-is-Camber-1a6c4e2fa5318049b6beef91b8ed7d1a?pvs=4

ABOUT OUR CULTURE:

Our mission to change behavioral health starts with us and how we operate. We don’t want to just change behavioral health, we want to change the way startups operate. Here are a few tactical examples:

1) Improving accessibility and quality of healthcare is something we live and breathe. Everyone on Camber’s team cares deeply about helping clinicians and patients.

2) We have to have a sense of humor. Healthcare is so broken, it's depressing if you don't laugh with us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Camber is hiring an Enterprise Strategy Associate to partner with our Director of Enterprise Revenue to build the narrative behind our largest client partnerships. Revenue cycle is the bloodline of a clinic, and through data, you build trust with the client. You will drive the narrative that helps a clinic understand the impact Camber can have on its business, and you’ll use it to shape the strategy of the deal.

This is not a traditional analyst role. You will follow a clinic through its entire time at Camber, from the first conversation to a fully rolled-out partnership, and keep driving the value of Camber at every step. You will join a team that values agency, intellectual honesty, and a “rowing in the same direction” mentality.

Your time will be split across three stages of the client journey:

 - Go-to-Market: You leverage a clinic’s data to build the narrative for how Camber can impact its revenue cycle, partnering with a Director of Enterprise Revenue on the analysis and story to win the deal.

 - Implementation: You are the subject-matter expert on both Camber and the clinic, and that expertise drives how we serve them. You help make sure the value of Camber is seen and understood as we roll out.

 - Stable State: You work with the strategic account management team to inform and prepare material for the clinic’s key decision-makers to help them understand the impact Camber is having on their business.


WHAT YOU’LL DO


BE THE ANALYTICAL AND NARRATIVE BACKBONE OF THE DEAL

 - Run Diagnostics: Dig into a clinic’s billing, claims, and payment data to find where revenue is being left on the table (e.g., denial trends, underpayments, aging AR, payer-specific patterns).

 - Build the Business Case: Size the opportunity in dollars and collection rate points, and build the ROI models that decision-makers use to say yes.

 - Drive the Strategy of the Deal: Use what the data says to decide where the deal goes: which problems to lead with, what each stakeholder cares about, and what a pilot needs to prove.

 - Build Executive-Ready Materials: Turn analysis into crisp, top-down stories that client leaders can act on and take to their own leadership.


IDENTIFY WHAT REALLY MATTERS

 - Ready the Internal Team: Surface what a new enterprise account or vertical will demand (e.g., net-new integrations, custom analyses, reporting needs) and get Product, Engineering, Data, and Operations ahead of it before go-live.

 - Flag Early: Act as the account’s early-warning system. When something in the data or the relationship looks off, raise it to the right people before it becomes a fire.


ANCHOR THE CLIENT ON CAMBER’S IMPACT

 - Own the Data Relationship: Be the go-to partner for the client’s data and analytics leads through the pilot and beyond.

 - Prove and Communicate Value: Track performance against the baseline and tell the story of Camber’s impact in recurring business reviews. Delivering results is half the job. Making sure the client knows about them is the other half.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience: 1–3 years in management consulting, investment banking, or strategy at a fast-moving startup.

 - Data Fluency: Experience working with large, messy data sets and turning them into conclusions that drive decisions.

 - Customer and Executive Exposure: Previous experience working directly with customers and senior executives.

 - Commercial Instinct: You understand how businesses make money and what motivates the people making the decision, and you can tie your analysis back to both.

 - Learning Velocity: Healthcare or RCM experience is a plus but not required. What matters more is that you do your homework, ask sharp questions, and ramp quickly into a complex domain.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - The ability to turn analysis into a narrative that moves a decision, not just a data dump.

 - “Client hands”: you’re comfortable and credible in front of a client, and you can hold your ground when the room pushes back.

 - A high bar for detail. Every number you put in front of a client is one you can defend.

 - High agency: you take ownership of ambiguous problems and create structure where none exists.

 - A collaborative spirit. You know when to pull in other teams, and you aren’t shy about asking for what you need.

 - Humility: you seeak out critique and get better because of it.


PERKS & BENEFITS AT CAMBER:

 - Comprehensive Health Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision plans with nationwide coverage, including 24/7 virtual urgent care.

 - Mental Health Support: Weekly therapy reimbursement up to $100, so you can prioritize the care that works best for you.

 - Paid Parental Leave: Up to 12 weeks of fully paid time off for new parents (birth, adoption, or foster care).

 - Financial Wellness: 401K (traditional & Roth), HSA & FSA options, and monthly commuter benefits

description:
The Patrick J. McGovern Foundation (PJMF) is a philanthropic organization dedicated to advancing artificial intelligence and data science solutions to create a thriving, equitable, and sustainable future for all. PJMF works in partnership with public, private, and social institutions to drive progress on our most pressing challenges, including digital health, climate change, broad digital access, and data maturity in the social sector.


ABOUT THE ROLE:
Strategic Capital is the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation’s grantmaking function. We fund nonprofits and civil society organizations using data science and AI to advance social good.
Portfolio Analysts help ensure that philanthropic resources are allocated effectively and with impact. They conduct research and analysis to identify and evaluate high-potential grant partners, perform due diligence through desk research, interviews, and financial reviews, and prepare materials to support final grant decisions. Analysts also monitor trends across the data and AI for good ecosystem, distill insights from existing grants, and contribute to learning that informs future investments. 
This position reports to the Director of Strategic Capital and offers an opportunity to shape how PJMF deploys capital to accelerate responsible and equitable technology solutions worldwide.

HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT:
Strategy Development
Develop and maintain a working understanding of PJMF’s grantmaking focus areas and the role of data and AI solutions within them.
Complete field sensing and landscape analyses that help PJMF stay abreast of new developments, opportunities, and shifts in the fields of AI and data science, and how they can be applied to drive social good.
Produce portfolio strategy retrospectives that synthesize outcomes, lessons, and directional insights from grant activity to inform future priorities.
Support the generation, validation, and refinement of strategic hypotheses and learning questions that guide PJMF’s philanthropic investments and deepen understanding of the field.
Grant Portfolio Development
Conduct research and outreach, and lead early-stage conversations, to identify nonprofit and civil society organizations whose work aligns with PJMF’s strategy and may be a fit for grant funding.
Prepare clear, evidence-based recommendation materials to support funding decisions.
Identify opportunities for collaboration and shared learning across grantees, portfolios, and adjacent fields to enhance collective impact.

description:
About TodayTix Group:
 
TodayTix Group (TTG) is the global e-commerce leader for cultural experiences, designing frictionless discovery and purchase journeys through innovative product design and industry-leading technology. Our portfolio of brands––including  TodayTix, New York Theatre Guide, London Theatre, Show-Score, Arthouse, Arthouse London, and Secret Cinema––connects millions of customers with the best in live entertainment.
 
Powered by vast data and insights, TTG helps theatres, producers, and cultural institutions reach highly engaged audiences and unlock meaningful revenue, transforming how tickets are sold across the world.
 
In 2025, TTG entered a new chapter as part of MARI, the global events and experiences company powering world-defining live experiences. Together, we’re expanding our reach, deepening our impact, and accelerating a shared vision to redefine the event lifecycle through seamless discovery, purchase, and engagement.
 
Life at TodayTix Group
We thrive in a nimble, growth-oriented environment where adaptability, curiosity, and a bias toward action help us stay ahead of the curve. We move quickly, iterate often, and expect everyone to take ownership of their impact - because we're building the future of live events, and there’s no script for what comes next.
 
New joiners are set up for success with a 90-day onboarding journey, complete with clear goals and measurable milestones. We believe feedback fuels growth, so we hold twice-yearly performance reviews focused on impact and development.
 
Above all, you’ll be working alongside a team of collaborative, passionate, and kind humans - people who love theatre and live experiences, and who support each other just as much as they challenge each other to do great work. 
 
We are seeking outstanding applicants of all backgrounds to join our team to bring new voices, talent, and perspectives to the table. We encourage all to apply.


What Success Looks Like:
- 
 Strategic Insight → You provide the executive team with a clear point of view and drive the strategic planning process, continuously assessing our growth opportunities and guiding the allocation of resources to those opportunities.   
- 
 Self-Directed Execution → You take ambiguous, half-formed problems and run them to ground. You scope the work, chase down the data and bring in the right people without waiting to be told or needing a blueprint. 
- 
 Institutional Influence → You become a trusted advisor to the executive team and brand General Managers, known for distilling complex financial puzzles into clear, actionable narratives that align with our growth objectives.
- 
 Measurable Impact → The deals and investments you underwrite perform against their underwriting case, and when they don’t, you’re first to know why.

What You’ll Do:
- 
 Underwrite Strategic Bets → Create comprehensive opportunity assessments for organic growth strategies that feed into TTG’s strategic roadmap, and coordinate business unit resources to execute these projects across the portfolio.
- 
 M&A Execution → Support the internal review of investment opportunities, including financial due diligence and forecasting, assessment of risks and opportunities, identification of integration and synergy realization strategies, and preparation of Investment Committee materials.
- 
 Commercial Partnerships & Investments → Underwrite and help negotiate strategic commercial partnerships and investments in live productions and experiences, including deals that secure exclusive ticketing for TTG. You’ll build the commercial model, pressure-test attendance and revenue forecasts, shape deal terms, and own the recommendation through to close.
- 
 Deal Sourcing → Maintain market maps and target pipelines across our core and adjacent verticals, and build relationships with bankers, founders and investors to support origination.
- 
 Board Materials → Prepare presentations on company performance, growth initiatives and prospective investments for meetings with the MARI Board of Directors.

We’re Looking for Someone With:
- 
 Top-Tier Foundation → You have 3–5 years of experience, ideally at a leading investment bank, strategy consulting firm, or corporate development team, where you have demonstrated success delivering rigorous analysis and "zero-defect" work products.
- 
 Commercial Judgment → You understand how businesses actually make money: unit economics, marketplace dynamics and competitive positioning. You form a point of view on where to play and how to win. 
- 
 Strategic Synthesis → You don't just "run the numbers"; you can turn divergent data sources into a high-conviction narrative that identifies the "so what" for our business and the wider industry.
- 
 Advanced Financial Modeling → You quickly and accurately build complex, dynamic financial models that serve as the foundation for capital allocation decisions.
- 
 Transaction Experience → You’ve worked on live deals, asking the hard questions in diligence, quantifying risks and synergies, and reading term sheets, LOIs and commercial contracts to assess the provisions that move value or shift risk. 
- 
 Applied AI Fluency → You use AI tools to accelerate the time-intensive parts of the job, and you bring the judgment that makes the output great. You know what an A+ work product looks like, and you push the tools until you get there. The result is work better than either you or the tools could produce alone.
- 
 Executive Presence → You are a confident communicator who holds their ground with senior leaders, takes a position, and changes minds with evidence.

Good to Know:
 
TodayTix Group takes care of our team. We’re proud to offer a generous suite of benefits and perks. Here are some of our favorites: 
 
-Hybrid work environment (blend of in-office and at-home days)
-Up to 4 weeks per year of flexible 'work from anywhere' 
-Healthcare, vision, and dental plans, with generous contributions from the company
-Life and disability insurance

REVENUE OPERATIONS LEAD

Location: USA Remote / San Francisco, CA · Full-Time

 


ABOUT ANDROMEDA

Andromeda is a market and infrastructure platform to buy, sell, and operate compute.

We believe demand for compute will grow exponentially. So fast that a handful of vertically integrated providers won't be able to scale across operations, capital, supply chains, and politics to serve it. The result is a massive wave of fragmentation, with AI factories of every shape and size coming to market to fill this demand. Our job is to enable all of that fragmented compute to flow through one platform, delivering reliable capacity to model builders, research labs, and inference providers when they need it. We believe every spare electron should be made productive for AI and we're building the platform that makes that possible.


We sit at the center of three forces:

 - Companies that need reliable, high-performance compute fast

 - A fragmented global supply of GPUs across hyperscalers, neoclouds, and independent data centers

 - Capital, risk, and operational complexity that most teams are not equipped to manage

When we succeed, trillions of dollars of compute will flow through Andromeda. Builders get capacity when they need it. Providers get a reliable way to monetize, operate, and finance infrastructure at scale. Capital gets an easy way to deploy, hedge, and underwrite.

In five years, Andromeda won't just participate in the AI infrastructure market. We will shape it.

 


THE ROLE

This is a chance to join Andromeda as our first Revenue Operations Lead — a strategic partner to Sales, Customer Success, and leadership as we scale a GPU compute market moving through its first real step-change in revenue. You'll own the operating system behind the number: pipeline hygiene, forecasting, deal desk process, supply administration, and the connective tissue between sales, supply, legal, and finance.

 

There's no playbook to inherit here. Our systems don't yet talk to each other the way they should, our routing and RACI are still being formalized, and the revenue org is being built from scratch. If you're an analytical operator who thrives in unstructured environments and loves bringing order to chaos, this role gives you the room to build it — and a path to leading revenue operations as the team grows.

● GTM tech stack: Own and optimize HubSpot (current CRM) — field standardization, data hygiene cadence, and integrations so deal blockers, supply status, and pipeline data actually stay in sync.

● AI-driven efficiency: Identify where AI tools and workflows can cut manual work out of reporting, forecasting, and deal ops — you'll be operating inside a team that already runs a lot of its own workflow through AI, and should be looking to extend that.

● Cross-functional glue: Sit at the intersection of sales, supply/ops, legal, and finance. Identify friction points in our business and get us unblocked.

 

What We’re Looking For

● Experience: 5+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or Business Operations at a high-growth B2B company — ideally one with usage-based, capacity-based, or infrastructure pricing (compute, cloud, hosting).

● CRM fluency: Hands-on CRM ownership at scale — you've built field architecture, workflows, and hygiene process, not just pulled reports.

● Systems thinking with a long-term view: You design for what a process looks like six months after go-live, not just whether it works on day one.

You will help design and build AI-enabled systems and workflows that improve the quality, speed, and repeatability of finance work.  The Associate Merchandise Planner will own the Women’s Plus Bottoms forecast from pre-season planning through in-season management, building financial plans, forecasts, and performance analyses that drive sales, inventory productivity, and profitability across Fix and Freestyle. Reporting to a Planning Manager, you’ll partner closely with Buying and collaborate with Allocation, Operations, Engineering, and Data Science to identify risks and opportunities, prepare decision-ready insights, and take action on the business. - Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment, balancing multiple priorities, incomplete information, and changing business needs while maintaining strong attention to detail and a bias toward action.
- This position may require the ability to sit for extended periods of time, use a computer or other office equipment, and communicate effectively (verbal and written).

- Experience in apparel, e-commerce, omnichannel retail, merchandise planning, allocation, or buying.
- Familiarity with Anaplan, Looker, SQL, BI tools, or retail planning systems.
- Experience using automation or AI-enabled tools to improve merchandise planning, forecasting, reporting, or repeatable workflows.

Join us in bringing joy to customer experience.  Five9 is a leading provider of cloud contact center software, bringing the power of cloud innovation to customers worldwide.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Account Strategy, this leader will provide hands-on support on live pursuits and help carry out the frameworks and programs for deal strategy.
 The Senior Account Strategy Manager diagnoses where a pursuit needs intervention, challenges the existing approach when it isn’t working, strengthens the customer value narrative and helps remove barriers to progress.

- Provide hands-on support across a portfolio of complex Enterprise and Strategic deals — spending the majority of time working directly with Sales Directors on live pursuits.

- Pressure-test the deal before it advances — refining the deal structure, modeling pricing options, building the business case, and shaping the negotiation plan, then presenting to senior approvers (Five9’s Delegation of Authority process) and engaging Partner Operations as needed.
- Contribute to core deal artifacts — proposals, implementation approaches, and commercial narratives — so Sales Directors can move pursuits with clarity and pace.
- Partner with Legal, Finance, and Revenue Operations in support of Sales Directors structuring, negotiating, and closing complex deals.
 Cross-Functional Alignment & Repeatable Execution

description:
Virta Health is on a mission to reverse metabolic disease in one billion people. Current treatment approaches aren’t working—over half of US adults have either type 2 diabetes or prediabetes, and obesity rates are at an all-time high. Virta is changing this by helping people reverse their metabolic condition through innovations in technology, personalized nutrition, and virtual care delivery reinvented from the ground up. We have raised over $350 million from top-tier investors, and partner with the largest health plans, employers, and government organizations to help their employees and members restore their health and take back their lives. Join us on our mission to reverse metabolic disease in one billion people.

As a Senior HEOR Scientist at Virta, you will play a pivotal role in proving and improving real-world health and economic outcomes for millions of patients. You will bridge cutting-edge outcomes research with commercial strategy by analyzing rich clinical and claims datasets to generate publication-grade evidence. Working cross-functionally across the data science, sales, marketing, and product teams, your work will directly shape how health plans, employers, and policy makers perceive and adopt virtual metabolic care.


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Lead the strategy, development, and execution of real-world evidence (RWE) programs and health economics models to demonstrate Virta's clinical and economic value proposition.

 - Translate complex real-world data (RWD) from health plans, employers, and external data warehouses into actionable operational and health economic insights that drive commercial growth, market adoption, and product innovation.

 - Publish findings in peer-reviewed scientific journals and present scientific evidence at national/international conferences, client presentations, and internal meetings.

 - Partner cross-functionally with sales, marketing, and product teams to integrate real-world evidence into commercial messaging, clinical care, and product development.

 - Serve as an internal subject matter expert, teaching HEOR methodologies to colleagues and advancing organizational research capabilities.


90 DAY PLAN

Within your first 90 days at Virta, we expect you will do the following:

 - First 30 Days: Onboard with the Clinical Research and Data Science teams, establish an understanding of Virta's data pipeline and existing evidence, and review current research compliance and privacy protocols.

 - First 60 Days: Take ownership of a claims dataset analysis project, collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders (Sales/Marketing) to align on evidence needs, and draft an updated HEOR strategy roadmap.

 - First 90 Days: Complete initial real-world evidence analyses, begin drafting a peer-reviewed publication or conference submission, and establish repeatable, AI-enabled workflows to streamline research and reporting tasks.


MUST-HAVES

 - Master’s degree or equivalent (PhD preferred) in Health Economics, Public Health, Pharmacoeconomics, or a related field.

 - 5+ years of experience analyzing claims/clinical datasets, publishing in peer-reviewed journals, and presenting economic outcomes of clinical programs.

 - 3+ years of business experience in a startup or high-growth environment, with proven ability to translate scientific evidence for commercial and marketplace applications.

 - Proficiency in SQL, Python, R, or SAS for conducting advanced claims analysis and data modeling.

 - Successfully designed and implemented repeatable AI-enabled workflows that address team bottlenecks and improve efficiency. For more information about AI usage in our hiring process, see Virta's AI Interview Resources page.


VALUES-DRIVEN CULTURE

Virta’s company values drive our culture, so you’ll do well if:

 - You put people first and take care of yourself, your peers, and our patients equally

 - You have a strong sense of ownership and take initiative while empowering others to do the same

 - You prioritize positive impact over busy work

 - You have no ego and understand that everyone has something to bring to the table regardless of experience

 - You appreciate transparency and promote trust and empowerment through open access of information

 - You are evidence-based and prioritize data and science over seniority or dogma

 - You take risks and rapidly iterate

Omni is the AI analytics platform that turns company data into a trusted source of truth for AI. If you like helping people get more from their data, come build with us. We’d love to hear from you.




THE ROLE

We are looking for a Strategic Finance Manager to own the quantitative core of our finance function. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role: you'll own the company financial model end-to-end, write the playbook for our core FP&A processes, and be the person who goes deep on the numbers behind major decisions.



You'll work directly with senior Finance leadership and functional leaders across the company. This isn't a support role — you'll take ownership of your work, handle novel problems independently, and improve our financial infrastructure as the business scales.



We're growing fast, so the model and the work are always changing. If you want to build and run complex financial systems at a company where your output is visible to leadership and shapes real decisions, this is the role.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Financial Model Own Omni's company financial model end-to-end: maintain the 5-year model, run scenario analyses, and build new components as the business evolves.

 - FP&A Cadence Run the core monthly and quarterly cycle: variance analysis, actuals-vs-budget reporting, and quarterly forecasting across the company. Partner with Accounting to keep financial data flowing cleanly into FP&A models.

 - 5-7+ years of experience in FP&A, investment banking, corporate finance, or consulting

 - Experience running FP&A workflows: variance analysis, budget vs. actuals, forecasting

 - Comfortable operating in a fast-moving startup where scope evolves

LOCATION

This is a fully remote role open to candidates based anywhere in the US.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Our Inference business works differently from a typical software business. What we can sell is capped by GPU fleet capacity, and what we earn depends on the blended cost of the GPUs serving each workload. Both can change week to week.

This role sits between the people who run the fleet and the people who sell it. You will be the person who can answer, at any point in the quarter, three questions with real numbers behind them:

 1. What do we have to sell?

You will own the commercial data, models, processes, and operating cadence behind these decisions, partnering closely with the Head of Digital Native Sales and serving as the commercial operating lead across Sales, Data Science, Inference Infrastructure, Finance, and Product.

This is a build role. Little of the commercial infrastructure you need exists today.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Capacity and demand

 - Translate customer requirements into structured inputs that Data Science and Inference Infrastructure can use to assess workload impact and feasibility, and help prioritize opportunities by revenue, margin, fit, timing, and strategic value.

Pricing and margin

 - Publish regular updates to GTM and Finance on available supply and recommended price, informed by market rates for provisioned throughput and per-token pricing.

 - Partner with Finance and Pricing to build rate cards, target prices, price floors, and discount guardrails GTM can act on.

Data infrastructure and GTM telemetry

Core revenue operations

 - Own territory design, ICP definition, data-driven targeting, pipeline management, forecasting, and compensation plan design for the Inference and Digital Native segment.

 - Track competitive dynamics across inference providers and adjacent players, turning them into pricing and positioning input.

Cross-functional leadership

 - Drive alignment across Sales, Data Science, Inference Infrastructure, Finance, and Product on demand, capacity, pricing, and economics.

title: Revenue Operations Lead
description:
REVENUE OPERATIONS LEAD



Harper is an AI-native commercial insurance company in San Francisco. We're not bolting AI onto insurance — we're rebuilding the entire business as software, on a simple bet: turning expert human judgment into compute is one of the largest transitions left to make, and a trillion-dollar industry still run 90% by hand is the place to prove it. We've grown ~100x in the last year and we move at that speed — on-site, in person, long days, very high standards. Almost no one joins Harper for insurance; they join to build the company that replaces how it works.






THE ROLE



Two dashboards disagree about the same funnel. A stage changed without the owner changing. The forecast moved and nobody can trace why. Those are not reporting annoyances. They are failures in the operating system you own.



Here is the honest state of it: Harper has been piecing RevOps together as it grew — a routing rule here, a dashboard there, a forecast someone built because the company needed one that week. It got us to ~100x growth. It will not get us through the next stage. We need someone who has actually run revenue operations before, who knows what a canonical funnel definition looks like and why a CRM automation needs a failure state, and who will take permanent ownership of the definitions, system behavior, routing, forecast, and instrumentation underneath Harper's revenue. When another team proves a temporary fix, you decide how it enters the permanent system, and you keep it reconciled.



Why now: Harper is scaling across three offices. Atlanta adds frontline volume, New York adds a second headquarters, and this San Francisco seat keeps one inspectable revenue system underneath all of it. This role does not own frontline sales management, customer conversations, placement strategy, or marketing creative. It owns the system those teams run on.






WHAT YOU'LL DO



 - Own the funnel definitions. Maintain the canonical meaning, entry rule, exit rule, source, and accountable owner for every revenue state, so there is one answer to what a stage means.

 - Own CRM behavior and routing. Define and maintain fields, validations, automations, permissions, and state transitions, and keep assignment logic, exceptions, ownership changes, and escalation paths inspectable and tested. Every routing change carries a test case, an approval owner, an effective date, and a rollback path.

 - Own the forecast. Publish the method, inputs, assumptions, and version, and carry the variance back to actual booked revenue every cycle.

 - Own revenue instrumentation. Make demand, contact, intake, quote, close, bind, and booked revenue reconcile to their source records for the same population and window.

 - Run funnel analysis and turn it into action. Find where volume, conversion, speed, or handoffs break, and convert the finding into a specific operating change with a named owner.

 - Automate repeat work with controls. Use enrichment, generated notes, task creation, quality checks, and reporting only when the source, resulting state, failure state, and human correction path stay visible.

 - Measure the change. Prove whether a workflow, campaign, routing decision, or sales motion moved conversion, speed, or revenue — and say so plainly when it didn't.






WHO YOU ARE



 - You have owned revenue operations, sales operations, or growth operations at a fast-growing company. This is the real background we've been missing, not a nice-to-have.

 - You understand CRM architecture, lifecycle stages, routing, attribution, forecasting, and pipeline hygiene from the inside.

 - You can write SQL, or work directly enough with the data to test a claim yourself before you repeat it.

 - You move from analysis to operating change and then measure whether the change worked.

 - You can partner with sales leaders and frontline operators — working inside the sales, intake, placement, and service workflows before changing them — without turning every problem into a process meeting.

 - You treat AI as leverage — you've operated generated notes, enrichment, routing, or reporting automations with visible source data, failure states, and correction paths — and you have opinions about where it helps and where it quietly corrupts the record.

 - You care more about booked revenue and conversion than dashboard activity.






THE REALITY — READ THIS BEFORE YOU APPLY



This job is on-site in San Francisco, Monday through Friday, long days, in the building with sales, intake, and placement, with travel to Atlanta and New York as the offices scale. You are inheriting a system that was assembled under pressure by people whose real jobs were something else. The first months are archaeology: finding every definition that drifted, every automation nobody owns, every report that doesn't reconcile, and fixing them while revenue keeps moving through the pipe. There is no pause button and no clean handoff.



If you want to administer a CRM without owning the revenue outcome, if you produce reports but don't make operating recommendations, if you want to own sales management, account placement, or marketing creative, or if you treat field completeness as proof that the underlying process works, this seat will frustrate you. It does not come with a remote or hybrid default. If the intensity reads as a cost you'd rather avoid, this isn't the seat. If it reads as the point, keep going.






COMPENSATION & LOGISTICS



 - Salary: 170,000–240,000 base, plus performance bonus and equity.

 - Equity: Yes.

 - Location: On-site, San Francisco. Based there or willing to relocate.

 - Schedule: Monday–Friday, long days. Exact coverage window is set by office.






BENEFITS



 - Health, dental, and vision insurance

 - Meals provided — breakfast, lunch, and dinner

 - Snacks, drinks, and coffee stocked daily

 - Commuter benefits

 - Free gym membership






PROCESS



 1. Team call — 30 minutes on Zoom. You meet the team, we meet you.

Your scope runs from raw merchant data through invoicing and financial reporting: the models that determine what gets invoiced and reimbursed, the financial models the business reports from, and the tie-outs that prove the numbers agree.

title: Revenue Operations Analyst
description:
OUR MISSION: HOSPITAL-QUALITY CARE, EVERYWHERE.

The healthcare industry still relies on faxes and phone tags to coordinate critical care for patients at home. We think patients and the clinicians who serve them deserve better than a system stuck in 1995.

Verse Medical is building the modern software infrastructure to make it happen. We're a well-funded Series C company (backed by General Catalyst, SignalFire, and Sapphire Ventures) on a mission to heal a fragmented system. Our platform connects the dots between providers, payors, and patients, ensuring people get the high-quality care they need, reliably and right where they live. We’re growing fast and looking for people who are driven by this mission to join us!




OUR VALUES: THE PRINCIPLES THAT GUIDE US

Our values are the operating system for how we work together and with our partners. They aren't just words on a wall; they are the principles we bring to every decision, every day.

 - We are transparent, upfront and direct. We operate with honesty and clarity. We share information openly, the good and the bad, and believe that direct, respectful feedback is the foundation of trust and progress.

 - We value speed of iteration. We are building something new, which means we learn by doing. We prioritize rapid iteration and getting solutions into the hands of users, believing that progress is more valuable than perfection.

 - We give 110% effort, 30% of the time. We are passionate about our mission, and there are moments that require us to go the extra mile. We believe in focused intensity when it counts, balanced by a sustainable pace that keeps our team energized for the long run.

 - We empathize with customers to a fault. When our users face a problem, we own it. Instead of asking them to change, we ask ourselves, "How can we make this better?" We believe true innovation comes from deep empathy and a relentless focus on solving the real-world challenges of healthcare.
   
   


THE OPPORTUNITY

Verse Medical is hiring a RevOps Analyst / GTM Engineer. This role is a critical hire as we build out the revenue operations function at Verse. This is one role with two halves. The analyst half answers the questions leadership cannot answer today: where pipeline comes from, where it stalls, and what the forecast actually is. The GTM engineer half builds the systems that stop those questions from being asked again: the Salesforce object model, the routing rules, the data pipelines, the automations and agents.



We sell to health systems, discharge planners, case managers, and post-acute partners, which means one health system is many locations and many referral sources rather than one account. That shape makes territory design, routing, and pipeline analysis harder than a typical logo-based motion, and worth doing well.



This is a hands-on individual contributor role with no team and no backlog waiting for you. If you want to write only SQL, or only administer Salesforce, this is not the right role. If you want to find a broken revenue process and fix it end to end, it is.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Pipeline and Forecast Operations

 - Run pipeline reviews, forecast calls, and weekly revenue reporting with accurate data, clear summaries, and tracked follow-up.

 - Monitor stage progression, conversion rates, sales cycle length, deal slippage, stale opportunities, close-date hygiene, and loss reasons, and say what they mean, not just what they are.

 - Partner with sales leadership and AEs to improve pipeline inspection, deal movement, and accountability without adding unnecessary admin work.

 - Own target account, territory, ownership, and routing logic as the team scales, including the fact that one health system is many locations and many referral sources, not one account.

 - Model quotas, capacity, and comp plans, and produce the numbers that pay people correctly.

CRM, Data, and AI-Native Operations

 - Own Salesforce as a system, not a database: object model, fields, validation rules, flows, and permissions. Make the CRM reflect how we actually sell.

 - Own day-to-day hygiene for required fields, lifecycle and stage accuracy, source attribution, account and contact quality, and data completeness.

 - Design, test, and roll out workflows that improve fill rates, enforce required fields, flag stale or low-quality data, and reduce manual cleanup.

 - Build and maintain dashboards for funnel conversion, rep activity, meetings, pipeline, forecast, and source performance.

 - Own the GTM stack end to end: what we buy, what we build, and how Salesforce, Gong, the warehouse, and outbound tooling talk to each other. Write the scripts and API integrations yourself.

 - Build internal AI tooling that puts answers in front of reps and leaders without them opening a report: account briefs, deal-risk alerts, automated CRM updates, Slack-native lookups. We already run agents against Salesforce and Gong, and you will extend them and decide what gets built next.

 - Use AI to compress the unglamorous work (data cleanup, enrichment QA, dedupe logic, first-pass analysis, documentation) and build the evaluation alongside it. An agent that is right 80% of the time and silent about the rest is worse than no agent.

 - Choose honestly between buying a tool, writing a script, and prompting a model, and be able to do the middle one yourself.

 - Document core GTM processes and handoffs across marketing, SDR, sales, finance, and enablement.

GTM Insights, Assets, and Operating Support

 - Act as the operational partner to Sales, Marketing, Finance, Enablement, and Clinical Operations. Translate each team's questions into data they can act on, and keep metric definitions consistent so they all work from the same numbers.

 - Support Finance on quota, capacity, commission exports, and board reporting; Marketing on attribution and source performance; Enablement with the data that shows where training is needed.

 - Support analytics across the full customer life

title: Revenue Operations & Strategy
description:
ABOUT TRAVERSAL

Traversal https://www.traversal.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com is the AI Site Reliability Engineer (AI SRE) for the enterprise.

Production complexity was already outpacing what engineering teams could manage manually, and AI-generated code is accelerating that gap. Traversal is built for that challenge, autonomously understanding and reasoning across even the largest, most complex production environments to diagnose, fix, and prevent incidents. Our mission is to free engineers from endless firefighting and give them more time to focus on creative, high-impact work.

Today, Traversal operates in mission-critical environments at some of the world’s largest enterprises, including PepsiCo, Nubank, Harvey, and DigitalOcean. Our roots remain deeply embedded in AI research, and we’ve brought together researchers from institutions including MIT, Harvard, Berkeley, Columbia, and Cornell with world-class technical staff and operators from companies like Google, Meta, Datadog, ServiceNow, and Citadel Securities to take on one of the hardest problems for AI to solve. Traversal is backed by Sequoia Capital, Kleiner Perkins, Redpoint Ventures, and Khosla Ventures.


THE ROLE

As a Revenue Operations individual contributor, you will be a force multiplier across our GTM organization. This is a broad, high-ownership role: you'll move fluidly between systems administration, analytics and forecasting, process design, and support for sales compensation and territory planning. You'll use an AI forward approach while working with sales, marketing, finance, and leadership to scale our the revenue engine.

This role suits someone who wants to own problems end-to-end — from diagnosing a broken process, to redesigning it, to building the Salesforce automation or dashboard that makes it stick — without a large team around them yet.




RESPONSIBILITIES

Systems & Data

 - Administer and continuously improve Salesforce: objects, automation, validation rules, and data quality, in partnership with the broader GTM tool stack (Claude, Clay, Apollo, Clari, Gong, Granola).

 - Own integration health across tools — investigating and resolving issues (e.g., sync errors, validation rule conflicts) that affect pipeline and forecast accuracy.

 - Maintain and improve reporting infrastructure and dashboards used by sales leadership and the executive team.

Analytics & Forecasting

 - Build and maintain pipeline and forecast models, capacity plans, and performance dashboards (e.g., cycle time by stage, pipeline coverage, conversion rates).

 - Partner with sales leadership to prepare board- and leadership-level pipeline and forecast materials.

 - Analyze funnel and rep performance data to surface trends, risks, and opportunities, and translate findings into recommendations.

Process & GTM Strategy

 - Build out the analytics layer that powers GTM decision-making, from pipeline dashboards to cohort analyses to efficiency metrics

 - Set the standard for how we analyze regional pipeline health, win/loss trends, and rep productivity, and determine how those insights feed back into the GTM plan

 - Partner with field leadership to diagnose gaps in the business and drive the structured plans to address them, covering real-time action as well as the insights that guide QBRs, pipeline reviews, etc.

 - Design and document processes and swim lanes that clarify handoffs across Sales, Marketing Ops, and Finance Ops.

 - Support go-to-market planning: territory design, account segmentation, and capacity/headcount modeling.

 - Design the coverage models aligned to 2-year growth projections, incorporating territory design, account segmentation, and capacity planning

 - Set the point of view on competitive dynamics, regional expansion priorities, and whitespace opportunities

Sales Compensation & Planning

 - Support the design and administration of sales compensation plans (quotas, commission structures, SPIFFs), ensuring plans are modeled accurately and compliant with relevant wage law.

 - Help resolve comp-related questions and disputes with clear, data-backed answers.

AI-Enabled Ways of Working

 - Use AI tools (Claude and similar) as a core part of the RevOps toolkit — automating recurring analysis and reporting, drafting process documentation, and prototyping solutions faster than manual approaches allow. As a company building AI-powered software, we expect our own operations to reflect that same leverage.


REQUIREMENTS

 - 7+ years of experience in Revenue/Sales Operations, Business Operations, or a related analytical role, ideally at a B2B SaaS company.

 - Deep hands-on Salesforce expertise (administration, automation, reporting) — you can build and troubleshoot, not just spec requirements for someone else.

 - Strong analytical and financial modeling skills with experience building forecast, capacity, or compensation models.

 - Demonstrated ability to work independently across ambiguous, cross-functional problems and drive them to resolution.

 - Excellent communication skills — comfortable presenting analysis and recommendations to senior leadership.

 - Experience with a modern GTM stack (Salesforce plus tools like Clay, Clari, Gong, Apollo, or similar).


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience at an early-stage or high-growth startup, building RevOps processes from scratch rather than maintaining existing ones.

 - Exposure to enterprise/strategic sales motions and long-cycle, multi-stakeholder deals.

SENIOR FINANCIAL ANALYST

Finance · Remote (US) · Full-time · Reports to Director of Finance




ABOUT NEST

Nest builds care plan infrastructure for veterinary hospitals. Corporate veterinary groups use Nest to run preventive care memberships under their own brand, and we handle what sits underneath: enrollment, recurring billing, analytics, marketing, and seller-of-record compliance.

Care plans change how pets receive care. Pet owners pay a predictable monthly amount, visit more often, and catch problems earlier. Hospitals build steadier revenue and longer client relationships. Our mission is to make that kind of preventive care available to every pet.




ABOUT THE TEAM

Finance at Nest is led by our Director of Finance and works closely with both founders and with leaders across Sales, Operations, Product, and Engineering. The team owns planning, board and investor reporting, and the financial models behind enterprise sales.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Our financial models have two audiences. Internally, they guide how we plan, hire, and raise capital. Externally, they help a large veterinary network decide whether to partner with us, and the EBITDA lift model and pricing proposal are often what a network's CFO evaluates before signing. You will spend about 70% of your time on FP&A and about 30% on customer-facing modeling. The work rewards people who ask why a number is what it is, can turn a vague question into a structured analysis, and care whether the reader understands the answer. After a year, you will own the operating model, the board package, and the standard enterprise proposal model, and the sales team will bring you into late-stage deals as a matter of course.




RESPONSIBILITIES

FP&A (about 70%)

 - Maintain and extend the operating model, including the revenue forecast, expenses, cash flow, and runway.

 - Prepare the monthly management report and the board package.

 - Lead model design and variance analysis for the annual budget and reforecasts, working directly with department leads.

 - Track unit economics by segment and by hospital, including acquisition cost, lifetime value, gross margin, and contribution margin.

 - Build investor-ready models, scenario analyses, and data room materials during fundraising.

 - Build and maintain management reporting and self-service dashboards in Sigma.

Customer-facing modeling (about 30%)

 - Maintain the EBITDA lift model and unit economics framework we present to enterprise prospects.

 - Model custom proposals across adoption levels, plan designs, fee structures, and rebates, showing the effect on both the customer's economics and Nest's margins.

 - Model revenue recognition for enterprise customers under ASC 606, including allocation, consumption-based recognition, straight-line amortization, and breakage.

 - Join customer calls when a CFO or procurement team wants to test assumptions on incrementality and ROI.

 - Analyze performance across our live hospitals, including spend lift, visit frequency, cancellations, breakage, and payment capture.
   
   


WHO YOU ARE

We are looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements for this role. If you meet them, we encourage you to apply. Preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.




MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

 - You have 4 or more years in FP&A, investment banking, consulting, or finance at a SaaS or healthcare company.

 - You build financial models that are clean, auditable, and ready to show a board or a customer.

 - You write your own SQL against a warehouse such as BigQuery or Snowflake.

 - You understand SaaS economics, including ARR, retention, CAC, LTV, and payback, and the accounting underneath them.

 - You have presented analysis to senior audiences and handled hard questions about it.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with Sigma, Looker, Tableau, or a similar BI tool.

 - Working knowledge of ASC 606 and subscription billing.

 - Experience with Stripe, QuickBooks, or similar billing and accounting systems.

 - Experience at a venture-backed company at seed or Series A.
   
   


HOW WE WORK

Nest is a small, fully remote team. Each person owns outcomes the company depends on, and the scope of most roles grows as the company does. We write decisions down, give direct feedback, and expect problems to be raised early. The work is demanding because hospitals and pet owners rely on it every day, and it suits people who want more ownership than a larger company would offer.





OUR HIRING PROCESS

Our process typically includes a conversation with the hiring manager, a working session based on the actual job, and conversations with the people you would work with most. We will tell you what each stage covers before it starts, and we close the loop with everyone we interview.




EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Role: Senior Data Analyst, Clinical Operations

Company: Atlas Oncology Partners

Location: Remote, with preference for Nashville or Boston

Travel: 10%

Position Type: Full-Time

Compensation: $90,000-$110,000 base, 10-15% bonus



About Us

Atlas is built for oncologists by oncologists. We provide practices with the staff, contracts, and toolkit they need to deliver truly whole person care to their cancer patients. Our value-based approach to care delivery aligns incentives, offering patients better outcomes, payors guaranteed reduction in medical expense, and provider partners greater financial independence.



Role Overview

Atlas has invested in a robust operations data infrastructure, and we're looking for someone who can build on that foundation to accelerate automation and speed-to-insight across our analytics workflows. The Senior Data Analyst, Clinical Operations will be a strategic analytics partner to clinical operations leadership, bringing together data from multiple platforms — including call center data, outcomes reporting, and our integrated Snowflake data warehouse that houses EMR data— to understand productivity and performance drivers across care teams. This role owns the full lifecycle of operational reporting: pulling and reconciling data across sources, reviewing it for accuracy and consistency, building and maintaining dashboards, and generating insights that practice administrators and leadership can act on.



Key Responsibilities



Data Integration & Quality

• Pull, combine, and reconcile data from multiple platforms into unified analyses

• Scope includes data supporting engagement, clinical programs, clinical documentation, and care team access/productivity

• QC data across sources to identify inconsistencies, gaps, or errors, and resolve or escalate data integrity issues as needed

• Maintain documentation of data sources, definitions, and report logic to ensure consistency across analyses

Reporting & Dashboards

• Build and maintain datasets to analyze care team productivity, call volumes/handling, and EHR-based workflow data across practice-partner sites

• Design, build, and maintain recurring dashboards and reports that track key operational metrics over time

Insights & Analysis

• Identify drivers of performance variation across teams, sites, and roles

• Generate clear, actionable insights from complex, multi-source datasets and present them to both technical and non-technical audiences, including clinic-level operators and senior leadership

Stakeholder Partnership

• Gather requirements from clinical operations leadership and translate them into specific, actionable analyses

Automation & Process Improvement

• To address all of the above responsibilities efficiently, individual should leverage modern tools and techniques (e.g., Excel Power Query, SQL, Claude)

• Identify opportunities to streamline and automate recurring analyses and scale reporting capacity across the organization



Reporting: This role will report to the VP of Clinical Operations



Required Qualifications

· Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Health Informatics, Business Analytics, Economics, or related) or equivalent practical experience

· 5+ years of experience in healthcare data analysis, with strong SQL proficiency and advanced Excel skills (complex formulas, pivot tables, data modeling)

· Experience working with EHR-sourced operational data and call center/IVR data in a healthcare or practice-operations setting

· Demonstrated ability to combine and QC data from multiple systems and build reliable, maintainable dashboards

· Ability to understand organizational goals and priorities and translate them into meaningful, trackable metrics

· Experience automating data and reporting processes using tools such as Power Query, SQL, and generative AI

· Familiarity with AI tools such as Claude or Copilot to support day-to-day analytical work

· Strong communication skills and comfort translating complex data into clear recommendations for non-technical stakeholders



Preferred Qualifications

· Familiarity with oncology or specialty care practice operations

· Experience with data visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI)

· Experience in a high growth startup

· Experience in outpatient value-based care primary care

· Health, Dental, Vision insurance

· Paid vacation, holidays, and sick leave

title: Capital Markets Analyst – Warehouse Finance
description:
We are a hybrid, remote-office company dedicated to growing our talent anywhere!
 We have onsite locations in: Sioux Falls, SD,  Phoenix, AZ,  Louisville, KY,  Troy, MI,  Franklin, TN,  Easton, PA.
 At Pathward, we take tremendous pride in our purpose to create financial inclusion for all™. We are a financial empowerment company that works with innovators to increase financial availability, choice, and opportunity for all.  We strive to remove barriers that traditional institutions put in the way of financial access, and promote economic mobility by providing responsible, secure, high quality financial products.
 We are a team of problem solvers and innovators who celebrate our differences and know that our unique perspectives make us stronger and well-positioned for success.  We celebrate, and embrace, our team members through our  *HUMBLE*HUNGRY*SMART  approach, and we believe that we are strongest when we embrace the voices of our employees, customers, partners, and the communities we serve. 
 About the Role: 
 Contribute to efforts to identify, evaluate and achieve strategic business opportunities through warehouse lending and new capital markets structured finance initiatives in order to optimize the bank’s balance sheet and improve the company’s financial performance. 
 What You Will Do: 
- Provides analytical and operational support in managing the bank’s warehouse lending business.
- Leads day-to-day warehouse lending operations and reporting responsibilities including preparing advance / paydown requests and reviewing borrowing base and compliance reporting.
- Assists in reviewing warehouse lending term sheets and legal documentation, assessing deal risk and return metrics, preparation of deal approval write ups, and presentations to the bank’s Executive Credit Committee.
- Develops and executes ongoing controls, mitigation plans, testing, and oversight of the warehouse lending business.
- Performs and presents periodic reviews on existing warehouse lending deals.

title: Senior Data Analyst, Strategic Finance
description:
At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it. 



As a Senior Data Analyst on the Finance team, you’ll play a pivotal role in uncovering the insights that shape company-wide planning, forecasting, and strategic decision-making. This high-impact role blends analytical rigor, technical fluency, and business acumen to steer strategy and identify opportunities for scalable growth.



The Finance Data team partners with both Finance and other teams across Vanta. You’ll collaborate closely with stakeholders to build trust and deliver data-driven recommendations; your work will influence everything from operating plans and investment decisions to self-serve reporting and process automation. This is a unique opportunity to deepen your analytics expertise in a dynamic, high-growth environment, with visibility into executive-level priorities and the ability to shape them with data.



What you’ll do as a Senior Data Analyst at Vanta:

 - Deliver strategic insights by conducting deep, prioritized analyses that inform high-impact financial decisions.

 - Act as a technical partner to teams across FP&A, Accounting, RevOps, Product, Marketing, and more.

 - Increase team efficiency by automating recurring deliverables and helping scale workflows as the company grows.

 - Empower decision-makers with self-service dashboards and data assets that surface trends and drive informed choices across the business.

 - Advance our analytics infrastructure by partnering with Data Engineering and other analytics teams to democratize access to high quality data and insights.



How to be successful in this role:

 - Experience: 4+ years of experience in data analysis or equivalent function. Exposure to FP&A, Accounting, or SaaS metrics is a plus.

 - Technical Skills: Strong proficiency in SQL and data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Sigma), with experience handling large and complex data sets. Familiarity with DBT is preferred. Bonus points for skill in Python for advanced analysis.

 - Analytical Thinking: Proven ability to analyze complex data sets, uncover key insights, and translate findings into actionable strategies that drive financial outcomes.

 - Collaboration: Demonstrated success working cross-functionally and building relationships across business teams. Comfortable engaging stakeholders with varying levels of data fluency.

 - Communication: Clear and effective communicator, both written and verbal. Skilled at presenting complex data insights to non-technical audiences.

 - Education: Bachelor’s degree in Data Analytics, Statistics, Informatics, Finance, Economics, Business, or a related field.

 - Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future employer sponsorship.

 - Open to using AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work - demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact.



What you can expect as a Vanta’n:

 - Industry-competitive salary and equity

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% of employee-only benefit premiums covered for most medical plans

 - 16 weeks paid Parental Leave for all new parents

 - Health & wellness stipend

 - Remote workspace, internet, and cellphone stipend

 - Commuter benefits for team members who report to the SF and NYC office

 - Family planning benefits

 - Matching 401(k) contribution with immediate vesting

 - Flexible PTO policy, plus 80 hours of Sick Time

 - 11 company-paid holidays

 - Virtual team building activities, lunch and learns, and other company-wide events!

 - Offices in SF, NYC, London, Dublin, Tel Aviv, and Sydney
   
   

To provide greater transparency to candidates, we share base pay ranges for all US-based job postings regardless of state. We set standard base pay ranges for all roles based on function, level, and country location, benchmarked against similar-stage growth companies. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors and may vary based on candidate location, skills, depth of work experience, and relevant licenses/credentials.  



#LI-remote



At Vanta, we are committed to hiring diverse talent of different backgrounds and as such, it is important to us to provide an inclusive work environment for all. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender identity, age, religion, sexual orientation, veteran or disability status, or any other protected class. As an equal opportunity employer, we encourage and welcome people of all backgrounds to apply.



About Vanta

We started in 2018, in the wake of several high-profile data breaches. Online security was only becoming more important, but we knew firsthand how hard it could be for fast-growing companies to invest the time and manpower it takes to build a solid security foundation. Vanta was inspired by a vision to restore trust in internet businesses by enabling companies to improve and prove their security. From our early days automating security monitoring for compliance standards like SOC 2, HIPAA and ISO 27001 to creating the world's leading Trust Management Platform, our vision remains unchanged. 

Now more than ever, making security continuous—not just a point-in-time check— is essential. Thousands of companies rely on Vanta to build, maintain and demonstrate their trust— all in a way that's real-time and transparent.



Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

description:
Why Rogo

Our mission is to transform global finance by empowering professionals at the world's top investment banks, private equity funds, and investment firms with AI that delivers unparalleled speed, accuracy, and insight. We're not just improving financial workflows; we're redefining them.

This is a unique opportunity to join a generational company driving transformation in one of the most important industries in the world. With a rapidly growing, global client base, proven product-market fit, and backing from world-class investors, we are scaling quickly and defining a new category of enterprise AI.

Our team is sharp, motivated, and deeply committed to Rogo’s mission. We take ownership of complex problems and stay relentlessly focused on our users. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, demand excellence, and want to help build the future of finance, we invite you to join us.


WHAT YOU WILL OWN

 - Rogo's Forward Deployed team consists of former bankers and investors who guide top financial institutions on how to apply AI in their day-to-day workflows and long-term strategy. You'll lead full-cycle client engagements, building consultative relationships and tailoring demos that resonate with investors and deal teams. Similar to how Solutions Architects secure the "technical win," you'll drive the "financial win" by translating Rogo's capabilities into real impact across banking and investing use cases.

 - Engage with bankers/investors at existing and prospective customers to understand and address their workflow challenges, and then explain and demonstrate the value of Rogo's AI solutions to address them.

 - Establish yourself as a credible expert in solving customers' specific problems (e.g., public company financial research, M&A advisory, company diligence workflows).

 - Lead product demonstrations tailored to the context of various financial firms, asking questions to validate how Rogo can add value and then showcasing Rogo's features and benefits relevant to each prospective client's potential use cases.

 - Partner with the marketing team to develop content that will resonate with bankers/investors, tailored to the unique needs of their practice areas and client types.

 - Act as the "Voice of the Customer," using your industry perspective to help the broader sales team develop and implement more effective strategies and synthesize customer feedback for the product team through a financial services lens.

 - Tailor the introduction of new solutions to specific customer needs.

 - Further the market perception of Rogo as uniquely credible, substantive, and helpful in applying its AI solutions to make bankers/investors better at their jobs.

 - Conduct research and analysis on customers and competitors.

What You Will Need

 - 3+ years of front-office experience at a large asset manager.  

 - Executive engagement skills and presence, with an ability to establish strong relationships with key decision-makers and build credibility at all levels.

 - Outstanding presentation skills, whether impromptu on a whiteboard or using presentations and demos.

 - Curiosity about AI's potential to transform financial services.

 - Sales or client-facing experience, including business development and/or experience directly managing institutional client matters and relationships.


WHO YOU ARE

 - You thrive in fast-paced environments. You are high-intensity and care a lot about what you do, and you're ecstatic to work at a startup. 

 - You are ambitious. You have fun solving problems that others think are impossible. 

 - You are curious.  You find joy in learning about AI, technology, and finance.

 - You are an owner. You are autonomous, self-directed, and comfortable working with ambiguity.

 - You are collaborative, organized, thoughtful, and kind.


WHY JOIN ROGO?

ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




THE STRATEGIC FINANCE TEAM

Examples of key problems the team is working on

 - Raise capital at the scale of a sovereign, not a startup. Powering 10s of GW will take hundreds of billions of dollars in debt and equity, a capital program that rivals a national infrastructure budget. You won't run a financing process; you'll assemble one of the largest pools of private capital in the industry.

 - Invent the instruments, don't pull them off the shelf. AI infrastructure is too new for the playbook to exist: credit support backed by equity warrants, hyperscaler-guaranteed leases, project finance underwritten against power and chips. You won't apply standard structures; you'll create the ones the rest of the market ends up copying. Few finance teams sit where energy markets, GPU supply, land control, and credit all converge.

 - Close at the speed of the build, not the speed of finance. Capital has to land in lockstep with gigawatts coming online: multiple landmark transactions running at once, on timelines most banks would call impossible. You'll redefine how fast serious capital can move.

 


ROLE SCOPE

 - Own financing execution across high-yield bond issuances, senior secured term loans, and equipment and project finance facilities, driving term sheet negotiation through close.

 - Structure, negotiate, and document credit support: guarantees, credit wraps, off-take agreements, and investment-grade backstops, and understand how each affects debt sizing and covenant mechanics.

 - Build and own transaction models: debt sizing, DSCR waterfalls, restricted payment mechanics, levered and unlevered returns, multi-scenario sensitivities. Be the team's check on model integrity across live deals.

 - Design and stress-test capital structures across HoldCo/OpCo/PropCo, cross-collateralization, cross-default, and intercreditor arrangements, and work with legal to turn structure into documentation.

 - Manage external counsel, financial advisors, and counterparty working groups, tracking open issues and pushing resolutions on deal timelines.

 - Own investor and lender materials: investment memos, lender presentations, bond offering documents, and internal approval packages.

You aren't just managing projects; you are critically evaluating how our business runs, leveraging data to challenge assumptions, and driving the hands-on execution of some of our most important strategic initiatives.

- Drive Strategic Initiatives: Execute on high-impact, 0-to-1 operational initiatives end-to-end. Investigate complex, ambiguous problems, develop rigorous work plans, and drive day-to-day execution.

- Synthesize Data into Strategy: Dig into raw business data (using Excel, SQL, or other systems) to reveal patterns and truths behind operational challenges. Translate these findings into clear, actionable recommendations for leadership and cross-functional partners.

- Unblock and Accelerate: Anticipate technical bottlenecks, call out trade-offs between business desires and constraints, and keep project teams aligned and moving forward.

- Analytical Tooling: Strong comfort with data. You should be highly proficient in Excel/Google Sheets and comfortable using SQL (or eager to leverage it) to query databases, join tables, and extract your own insights.
- Education: BA or BS degree (or equivalent practical experience).
- Natural Systems Thinker: You intuitively see how different parts of an organization, workflow, and technology stack interconnect. You don't build temporary "band-aid" fixes; you design systems that hold complex, interdependent relationships in balance.

- Collaborative & Growth-Minded: You love being in rooms with brilliant people who challenge you. Instead of feeling intimidated, you use those environments as fuel to grow, learn, and elevate your own capabilities.
